projects.name: langchain-nextjs-template
projects.tagline: Next.js routes for LangChain.js chat, agents, structured output and RAG
projects.summary: Five Next.js API routes that each show one LangChain.js pattern: plain chat, Zod structured output, a prebuilt LangGraph.js agent with Tavily search, and RAG as a chain and as an agent over a Supabase pgvector table. Tokens stream to the client through the AI SDK, routes run on Edge functions, and there is no auth or persistence beyond the vector table. For developers learning LangChain.js who want runnable routes to copy.
strengths: Each pattern is one route file you can lift into your own app
Hosted demo on Vercel
Mock-backed integration tests run without API keys or a live database
Supabase adapter reuses the documents table and match_documents function; no migration
weaknesses: No auth and no chat history persistence
OpenAI only out of the box; other providers need code changes
Re-ingesting the same text duplicates vectors; no dedupe
Agent and search examples need a Tavily key

projects.name: chatbot
projects.tagline: Next.js chat template with Auth.js, Postgres history and AI Gateway models
projects.summary: Clone it and you get a Next.js App Router chat app on the AI SDK with Auth.js login, chat history in Neon Postgres through Drizzle migrations, file uploads to Vercel Blob and a streaming UI on shadcn/ui. Models route through Vercel AI Gateway; Mistral, Moonshot, DeepSeek, OpenAI and xAI are preconfigured in lib/ai/models.ts. For teams starting a chat product on Vercel who want auth and persistence wired on day one.
strengths: Auth.js, Postgres chat history and Drizzle migrations wired out of the box
Live demo plus a separate docs site
Per-model provider routing in lib/ai/models.ts; swapping vendors is a small edit
Tests included
weaknesses: Defaults to Vercel services: AI Gateway, Neon Postgres, Vercel Blob
Off Vercel you must set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and replace Blob storage
No Docker or compose files

projects.name: chat
projects.tagline: Nuxt UI chat template with GitHub login, SQLite history and AI Gateway
projects.summary: A Nuxt app on Nuxt UI and the AI SDK: streaming replies with reasoning, three models through Vercel AI Gateway (Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5 Nano), provider web search, dictation over WebSocket, and chart and weather tool calls. GitHub OAuth, chat history in SQLite or Turso through Drizzle, and NuxtHub Blob uploads are included. For Vue and Nuxt teams who want a complete chat UI with persistence.
strengths: Auth, Drizzle migrations and uploads wired; local dev needs no external database
Blob storage swaps between local disk, Vercel Blob, Cloudflare R2 and S3
Live demo and a one-command scaffold (npm create nuxt -t ui/chat)
Committed within the last day
weaknesses: Models and dictation go through Vercel AI Gateway; direct keys need code changes
Auth is GitHub OAuth only
No tests listed
Production database path assumes Turso

projects.name: claude-quickstarts
projects.tagline: Independent Claude API starter projects, one folder per pattern
projects.summary: Independent Claude API starter projects in one repo, not one app: a customer support agent with a knowledge base, a financial data analyst with charts, computer-use and Playwright browser-use demos, a two-agent coding loop on the Agent SDK, and Managed Agents examples for Slack, Linear, Sentry, MCP and CopilotKit AG-UI. Mixed Next.js and Python, each folder with its own setup. For developers copying out one pattern.
strengths: Covers computer use, browser use, Agent SDK and Managed Agents in one checkout
Each quickstart is self-contained with its own README and setup
Tracks current toolset shapes (computer_toolset_20260801, browser_toolset_20260801)
Ships a CLAUDE.md for agent-driven edits
weaknesses: Not a single forkable app; you extract one subfolder
No auth, billing or database at the root; only what each sample needs
Anthropic-only; no provider abstraction
No root .env.example or Docker files

projects.name: gemini-chatbot
projects.tagline: Next.js chatbot template defaulting to Gemini with NextAuth and Postgres
projects.summary: An earlier cut of the Vercel chatbot template pinned to Google Gemini: Next.js App Router, AI SDK streaming with tool calls, NextAuth.js login, chat history in Vercel Postgres through Drizzle, and file storage on Vercel Blob. The default model is gemini-1.5-pro; the AI SDK lets you switch to OpenAI, Anthropic or Cohere. For teams on Google models who want the Vercel chat stack.

Two env vars to deploy: AUTH_SECRET and GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY
Deployed demo at gemini.vercel.ai

Tied to Vercel Postgres and Blob; self-hosting means swapping both
No tests, no Docker
vercel/chatbot is the maintained successor for most uses

projects.name: twitterbio
projects.tagline: Single-form Next.js text generator streaming from Together AI
projects.summary: A one-page Next.js app: a form builds a prompt, sends it to Together AI and streams the reply back, with two open models wired (Qwen 3.5 9B with thinking off, GPT OSS 20B with a reasoning indicator). Nothing else is included: no auth, no database, no tests. For developers who want the smallest prompt-to-text starter to grow from.
strengths: One env var (TOGETHER_API_KEY) and it runs
Shows streaming for both a direct model and a reasoning model
Deployed live example at twitterbio.io
weaknesses: No auth, database, rate limiting or tests
Tied to Together AI; no provider layer
Single feature; most of a product is still to build

projects.name: ai-chat

For Laravel teams who want a chat base in their own stack.
strengths: Installs with laravel new --using=pushpak1300/ai-chat
Auth, chat sharing and SSE streaming already wired
Adding a provider or model is one enum case
Tests included

No Docker files
PHP 8.3+ and Composer required

projects.name: zola
projects.tagline: Multi-provider chat UI on Next.js with Ollama detection and BYOK
projects.summary: A Next.js chat interface on the AI SDK that talks to OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Gemini and local Ollama models, with bring-your-own-key through OpenRouter. Supabase handles auth and file storage once you follow INSTALL.md, a docker-compose file pairs it with Ollama, and Zola is a running product (zola.chat) you fork rather than a scaffold. For builders who want a finished multi-model chat UI to brand.
strengths: Runs with one key or with local Ollama only; no database required for that path
docker-compose.ollama.yml included; auto-detects local Ollama models
Hosted instance at zola.chat shows the exact UI you get

README marks it beta; MCP support is work in progress
No tests listed
Last commit 2025-12; check activity before forking

projects.name: openai-chatkit-advanced-samples

projects.summary: Four ChatKit scenarios, each a FastAPI backend on the ChatKit Python SDK plus a React frontend: a virtual-cat caretaker, an airline support concierge, a newsroom assistant and a metro-map planner. Together they exercise server and client tools, widgets with actions, attachments, dictation, annotations, @-mentions and composer commands. For teams writing a custom ChatKit server who need a reference per feature.
strengths: Feature index maps every ChatKit capability to the file that implements it
Each demo starts with one command on its own port (5170 to 5173)
Attachment upload and dictation are implemented end to end

Python backend plus Node frontend; needs uv and npm
OpenAI-only

projects.name: openai-chatkit-starter-app
projects.tagline: Minimal self-hosted and managed OpenAI ChatKit reference apps
projects.summary: Two reference apps for embedding OpenAI ChatKit: one self-hosted integration where you run the ChatKit backend yourself, and one managed integration that connects the widget to a hosted Agent Builder workflow. The root README is a two-line index, setup lives in each subfolder, and seed data lists Next.js plus Python. For teams committed to ChatKit who want the smallest working wiring.

Shows self-hosted and managed hosting modes side by side
weaknesses: Root README has no setup, env or port details
No auth, database, tests or Docker
Locked to OpenAI ChatKit and Agent Builder

projects.name: openai-responses-starter-app
projects.tagline: Next.js chat on the OpenAI Responses API with hosted tools
projects.summary: A Next.js chat UI wired to the OpenAI Responses API with streaming, multi-turn state, function calling and the hosted tools: web search, file search over a vector store you create from the UI, and code interpreter. For developers building an assistant on OpenAI hosted tooling.

Working OAuth example for OpenAI first-party connectors (Calendar, Gmail)
Custom functions live in config/functions.ts; clear extension point

No auth, persistence or tests
MCP servers that need auth are left to you

projects.name: langgraph-fullstack-python

Opens directly in LangGraph Studio

No auth
Default model string claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 is dated
Server-rendered FastHTML UI; limited for rich client-side features

projects.name: azure-search-openai-demo
projects.tagline: Azure RAG chat reference on AI Search and Azure OpenAI

For teams already on Azure.

Evaluation, safety evaluation, monitoring and productionizing guides in docs/
Multimodal, speech and agentic retrieval are switchable features
Commits within the last week; tests included

Provisions paid services by default (AI Search, Document Intelligence); run azd down
Azure OpenAI only; no other provider path
README itself says not production-ready without extra security work

projects.name: rag-postgres-openai-python
projects.tagline: RAG over Postgres table rows with hybrid search and SQL filters
projects.summary: A FastAPI backend and React frontend that answer chat questions about rows in a PostgreSQL table. Retrieval is hybrid (pgvector similarity plus full-text search fused with RRF), an OpenAI function call turns phrases like cheaper than 30 dollars into WHERE clauses, and it runs against Azure OpenAI, OpenAI.com or Ollama; azd deploys it to Container Apps with managed identity. For teams whose knowledge is structured rows, not documents.
strengths: Hybrid vector plus full-text search with RRF is implemented in SQL, not a vendor service
Provider switch by env var: Azure OpenAI, OpenAI.com or Ollama
Evaluation, safety evaluation and load-testing docs included
Tests included; dev container and Codespaces configs
weaknesses: Deploy path is Azure-only (azd, Container Apps, Flexible Server)
Local run expects Postgres 14+ with pgvector installed yourself
Sample schema is one products table; multi-table questions need new code
No auth in the app itself

projects.name: llm-app
projects.tagline: Pathway RAG pipeline templates that re-index live data sources
projects.summary: Eight Dockerized Python pipelines on the Pathway framework: question-answering RAG, a live document indexer, multimodal RAG with GPT-4o, unstructured-to-SQL, adaptive RAG, a private Mistral plus Ollama variant, slide search and video RAG. Each watches a source (file system, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka, Postgres), keeps an in-memory vector and full-text index current and serves an HTTP API. For teams whose documents change constantly.
strengths: No separate vector DB, cache or API framework; indexing is in-process (usearch, Tantivy)
Connectors for file system, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka and Postgres with live sync
Private variant runs fully local with Mistral and Ollama
Docker images and tests included
weaknesses: Pathway is the real dependency; its Rust engine is opaque to most Python teams
Pipelines are backends; the UI is an optional Streamlit demo
Root README has no setup; each template README is required reading
Index lives in memory; sizing for millions of pages is on you

projects.name: chat-langchain

Supabase token plus guest identity handled in identity.py

Tests included
weaknesses: Tied to Managed Deep Agents (mda CLI) for identity, ingress and state
Needs a Pylon account and knowledge base ID to run as written
Docs retrieval depends on a managed MCP connector, not your own index
Product-specific: you replace the LangChain docs with your own corpus

projects.name: chat-with-your-data-solution-accelerator

Admin UI for ingesting documents and editing prompts without code changes
Two selectable orchestrators: Agent Framework or LangGraph

README calls it a starting point, not production-ready

projects.name: azure-search-openai-javascript

projects.summary: The Node.js counterpart of the Azure RAG sample: a search API, an indexer service and a web app that answer chat and Q&A questions over your documents with citations, using Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI through LangChain.js. azd up provisions Container Apps for the backend and a Static Web App for the frontend, and the search API speaks the AI chat HTTP protocol so the Python backend can replace it. projects.name: SupabaseAuthWithSSR

Per-step token and cache usage stored on messages; user and admin cost dashboards

projects.name: llm-answer-engine
projects.tagline: Perplexity-style Next.js answer engine over Brave search results
projects.summary: A Next.js app that takes a question, pulls results from Brave Search and Serper, scrapes the top pages with Cheerio, chunks and embeds them with OpenAI embeddings, and streams an answer from Groq (Mixtral by default) with sources, images and follow-ups. docker compose and a standalone Express API variant included
Optional rate limiting and semantic cache via Upstash

projects.name: nextjs-openai-doc-search
projects.tagline: Build-time embeddings of your MDX docs into Supabase pgvector
projects.summary: A Next.js starter that chunks the .mdx files in pages/ at build time, embeds each section with OpenAI and stores vectors in Supabase pgvector, skipping files whose checksum has not changed. At runtime an Edge function embeds the question, runs a similarity search and streams a completion with the matched sections in the prompt; the schema ships as a Supabase migration. For teams adding chat search to a Next.js docs site.
strengths: Checksum table avoids re-embedding unchanged files on every build
pgvector schema is a checked-in Supabase migration
One secret (OPENAI_KEY) when deployed with the Vercel Supabase integration
weaknesses: Uses the legacy OpenAI text completion endpoint; expect to port it
Only .mdx in pages/ is indexed; other sources need code
No auth, no conversation history, no tests
Design dates from 2023; last commit 2026-05

projects.name: openai-support-agent-demo

projects.name: eve-software-factory-template

projects.name: Background Agents
projects.tagline: Background coding agents on cloud sandboxes with Slack, GitHub and Linear triggers
projects.summary: Runs coding sessions in cloud sandboxes coordinated by a Cloudflare Workers control plane, driven from a web UI, Slack, GitHub PR comments, Linear issues or webhooks. Sessions use OpenCode or the Claude Agent harness with Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, DeepSeek or Z.AI models, with multiplayer editing, commit attribution, child sessions and cron or event automations. For single-tenant engineering orgs.
strengths: Snapshot restore, prebuilt images and proactive warming for fast session starts
Automations from cron, Sentry alerts, GitHub workflow runs and inbound webhooks
Secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM and scoped globally, per repo or per environment
Browser automation, code-server and a web terminal inside each sandbox
weaknesses: Single-tenant only; all users must be trusted members of one organization
Control plane requires Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects and D1
Sandboxes run on third-party providers (Modal, Daytona, E2B, OpenComputer, Vercel)
Cached credentials can persist in snapshots; grant removal does not revoke tokens

projects.name: vibe-kanban
projects.tagline: Kanban board that runs coding agents in per-issue git workspaces
projects.summary: Vibe Kanban pairs a kanban board for planning with workspaces where coding agents execute, each with its own branch, terminal and dev server. You review diffs, leave inline comments that go back to the agent, preview the app in a built-in browser, and open pull requests. The README announces the project is sunsetting.
strengths: Works with 10+ agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Amp and Cursor
Starts with one command: npx vibe-kanban
Inline diff comments are sent straight to the agent
Built-in preview browser with devtools, inspect mode and device emulation
weaknesses: README states the project is sunsetting
Last release was 2026-04-24, months before the latest commit
Each coding agent must be installed and authenticated separately
Maintainers ask that PRs not be opened without prior discussion

projects.name: warp
projects.tagline: Terminal-based development environment with a built-in coding agent
projects.summary: Warp is a Rust client that started as a terminal and now includes a built-in coding agent. It can also run third-party CLI agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI. The client source is public, and the repository is itself maintained partly by automated agents (Warp Factories).
strengths: Runs its own agent or external CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI)
Client source is public; build with ./script/bootstrap and ./script/run
UI framework crates (warpui_core, warpui) are MIT-licensed
Written in Rust; contribution flow and AGENTS.md engineering guide documented
weaknesses: Most code is AGPL-3.0, which constrains proprietary forks
README does not state supported models, RAM or GPU requirements
Factories automation is early access with a demo booking flow
README covers only the client; server-side components are not described

projects.name: continue
projects.tagline: Coding agent as a CLI, VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin
projects.summary: Continue is a coding agent distributed as an npm CLI, a VS Code extension (Marketplace and OpenVSX) and a JetBrains plugin. The repository is read-only and no longer actively maintained; the final 2.0.0 release removed anonymous telemetry and authentication. The README does not list supported models or providers and points to docs.continue.dev for configuration.
strengths: Ships as CLI, VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin from one codebase
Final 2.0.0 release removed anonymous telemetry and authentication
Apache-2.0 license; extension available on OpenVSX as well as Marketplace
Source for each extension lives in its own directory (vscode, cli, intellij)
weaknesses: Repository is read-only and no longer actively maintained
README recommends the CLI over the JetBrains plugin
README does not list supported models or providers; docs needed
No Docker or compose setup

projects.name: grok-build
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent from SpaceXAI with a full-screen TUI, written in Rust
projects.summary: Grok Build is the source for the `grok` CLI, a full-screen terminal agent that reads your codebase, edits files, runs shell commands and searches the web. It runs interactively, headlessly for scripts and CI, or inside editors through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). The bundled user guide covers MCP servers, skills, plugins, hooks and sandboxing.
strengths: Three run modes: interactive TUI, headless for scripting and CI, and ACP for editors
Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows via a one-line install script
Supports MCP servers, skills, plugins and hooks, per the bundled user guide
Apache-2.0 first-party code, with third-party notices documented in the repo
weaknesses: External contributions are not accepted
Repo is synced periodically from a private monorepo, not developed in the open
Browser authentication on first launch; supported models are not listed in the README
Windows source builds are untested; building needs DotSlash and protoc

projects.name: Tabby
projects.tagline: Self-hosted code completion and chat server for IDEs
projects.summary: Serves code completion and chat to VS Code, Vim and JetBrains extensions from one self-contained binary with no external database. Runs local models such as StarCoder-1B and Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct on CUDA or Apple Metal, exposes an OpenAPI interface on port 8080, and adds an Answer Engine, repository and GitLab merge-request indexing and LDAP auth. For teams that want an on-premises Copilot alternative.
strengths: Single binary with embedded storage; no DBMS or cloud service required
One docker run command starts a server with completion and chat models
Repository context indexing, GitHub and GitLab integration, LDAP auth, usage reports
Live demo instance and documented extensions for VS Code, Vim and IntelliJ
weaknesses: Last commit June 2026; recent news points to the separate Pochi agent
License is non-standard (GitHub reports NOASSERTION); check terms before deploying
Model list and hardware guidance live only in the external docs
Building from source needs Rust, protobuf and OpenBLAS

projects.name: aider
projects.tagline: Terminal pair-programming tool that edits your git repo with LLMs
projects.summary: Aider runs in the terminal and edits files in an existing codebase through chat with a cloud or local LLM. It builds a map of the repository to give the model context, commits each change to git with a generated message, and can run linters and tests after edits and try to fix failures. It also accepts images, web pages and voice input, and can be triggered by comments in an editor.
strengths: Auto-commits every change to git, so diffs and undo use ordinary git tools
Connects to almost any LLM, including local models
Runs linters and tests after edits and attempts to fix reported failures
Repo map gives the model context across larger codebases
weaknesses: Terminal-first; no standalone GUI, IDE use relies on comment watching
Last tagged release is 2025-08-09, older than recent commits
Needs an LLM API key or a separately hosted local model
Installed via pip and aider-install; no Docker setup in the repo

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: Agent skills for planning, TDD, debugging and code review
projects.summary: A collection of Markdown skill files for coding agents, split into engineering and productivity groups. It covers grilling sessions that build a project glossary and ADRs, spec and ticket generation, red-green-refactor TDD, a bug diagnosis loop, and diff review. Installs as a plugin for Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot, via gemini skills install for Gemini CLI, or as editable files through npx skills.
strengths: Small, composable skills that can be edited; README says they work with any model
Plugin install for Claude Code, Codex and Copilot, with automatic updates
Setup skill configures issue tracker (GitHub, GitLab, local files), triage labels and doc locations
Separates user-invoked orchestration skills from model-invoked discipline skills
weaknesses: Manual updates for Gemini CLI and npx installs
Installing both plugin and npx copies gives every skill twice
Must run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once per repo before the engineering skills
Architecture skill is a survey only and will not untangle an old codebase

projects.name: ecc
projects.tagline: Agents, skills, hooks and rules bundle for Claude Code, Codex and other harnesses
projects.summary: ECC installs a plan, test, implement, review, verify workflow into coding agents. It ships 71 agents, 311 skills, 97 legacy command shims, hooks, selectable rules, session memory and the AgentShield scanner for prompts, hooks, MCP config and permissions. Native plugin paths exist for Claude Code and Codex; Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed and others get capability-limited adapters.
strengths: Large bundle: 71 agents, 311 skills, hooks and rules in one install
Guided setup wizard for Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code with dry-run mode
Includes AgentShield scanning of MCP config, permissions, hooks and secrets
MIT licensed; npm releases pinned per version tag
weaknesses: Feature parity varies; non-Claude harnesses are capability-limited adapters
Claude plugins cannot ship rules, so rule packs need a manual copy
Stacking install methods duplicates skills and hooks; README warns against it
Private-repo GitHub App is paid (from $19/seat/month)

projects.name: caveman
projects.tagline: Proxy and skill that cut token use in coding agents
projects.summary: Caveman has two parts. A local proxy compresses what coding agents read (logs, CSV, YAML, JSON, test output, web pages), and a skill makes the agent reply in terse, answer-first text while code, paths and numbers stay verbatim. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider and 30+ other agents, and ships SDK middleware for the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, OpenAI and Anthropic.
strengths: Proxy cut whole-session input tokens 33.2% in its own 54-run Claude Code benchmark
Skill-only install via `npx skills add`, no proxy needed
README lists losing cases: HTML got 9.9% worse, and the per-request billing caveat
TypeScript and Python middleware wraps existing LLM SDK calls
weaknesses: No HTML compressor yet; the benchmark HTML session used more tokens
CLI sends usage telemetry by default; opt out with `caveman telemetry off`
Proxy needs Node.js 22.13+
Skill rules add about 1,160 tokens; cost impact with caching not measured

projects.name: ponytail
projects.tagline: Skill prompt that makes coding agents write less code and add tests
projects.summary: Ponytail is a single prompt (SKILL.md, with a compact AGENTS.md) that loads into coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. It tells the agent to check existing code, the standard library and native platform features before writing anything, and adds /ponytail-review, /ponytail-audit and /ponytail-debt commands. The README reports 53% less code and 45% fewer tokens in its own 39-task benchmark.
strengths: Works with 20 agents; plugin install for Claude Code and Codex, AGENTS.md for others
Benchmark method and per-task tables are published in the repo
Keeps validation, security and accessibility; leaves a small test for risky logic
No config file required; default level can be set by env var or JSON file
weaknesses: Benchmark figures are self-reported, run in Claude Code with Opus 5.5 only
Slash commands need a skill-capable host; rule-file adapters get only the always-on prompt
Cursor with hooks supports only /ponytail level switching, not review or audit
README is heavy on banners and a waitlist, with a jokey tone

projects.name: spec-kit
projects.tagline: CLI and agent skills for spec-driven development, bug fixing and idea assessment
projects.summary: Spec Kit is a Python CLI (`specify`) that installs templates and slash-command skills into a project so a coding agent follows a fixed process. It ships spec-driven development in core (constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement, converge). Bug fixing and idea assessment are opt-in extensions that write reports under `.specify/`.
strengths: Works with multiple coding agents via an integration key, e.g. `--integration copilot`
Process outputs are Markdown artifacts stored in the repo under `.specify/`
Bug-fix flow separates assess, fix and test, ending in a verified, partial or failed verdict
Extensions, presets, workflows and bundles let you customize or replace processes
weaknesses: Needs Python 3.11+ and uv installed
Skills run in the agent's chat, not the terminal; syntax varies by agent
Bug fixing and assessment require a separate `specify extension add` step
Provides no model or agent itself; a supported coding agent is required

projects.name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
projects.tagline: Design-system skill that gives coding agents searchable UI styles, palettes and fonts
projects.summary: An agent skill that runs a local Python search script (BM25 ranking, standard library only) over CSV datasets of UI styles, color palettes, font pairings, landing patterns and UX guidelines. Given a product description, it applies 192 industry reasoning rules and outputs a design system with pattern, style, colors, typography, anti-patterns and a checklist. An npm CLI installs it for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and about 20 other assistants.
strengths: Scripts use only the Python standard library and make no network calls
One CLI (uipro init --ai) installs to over 20 assistants, per project or globally
Data is plain CSV: 79 styles, 192 palettes, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines
Covers 22 stacks including React, Next.js, Vue, SwiftUI, Flutter and Jetpack Compose
weaknesses: Requires Python 3 on the machine; the agent will not install it for you
Brand identity, logo, CIP and image-generation features are in the paid premium version
Recommendations are rule and keyword matches; output quality depends on the agent using it
Only 50 of 79 styles are active in normal recommendations

projects.name: superpowers
projects.tagline: Skill set that enforces a plan-and-TDD workflow in coding agents
projects.summary: Superpowers is a library of composable skills plus a bootstrap skill (using-superpowers) that makes a coding agent brainstorm a spec, write a task plan, and implement it with subagents under red/green TDD and code review. It installs as a plugin or extension for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and others. Skills trigger automatically.
strengths: Installs via plugin marketplaces or one command on 15+ listed agent harnesses
Covers the full loop: brainstorming, worktrees, plans, subagent execution, review, branch finish
diagnosing-superpowers skill reads session transcripts and can export a scrubbed bug bundle
MIT licensed, with eval harness and plugin tests in the repo
weaknesses: Workflows are mandatory, so small tasks go through the same process
Subagent-driven mode costs more tokens than inline execution
Install is per harness; each agent needs separate setup
Optional visual companion loads a vendor-hosted logo that reports version unless disabled by env var

projects.name: agent-skills
projects.tagline: Markdown skill pack and slash commands for the software lifecycle in coding agents
projects.summary: A set of 25 SKILL.md workflows covering spec, plan, build, test, review and ship, plus 9 slash commands, 4 agent personas and reference checklists. Skills are plain Markdown with steps, verification gates and anti-rationalization tables. They install into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and others via the skills CLI or native plugin commands.
strengths: Installs into 70+ agents with one `npx skills add` command
Each skill has explicit steps, verification gates and exit criteria
Native plugin installs for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Gemini CLI
Skills are plain Markdown, usable with any agent that reads instruction files
weaknesses: Slash commands like /spec and /build are Claude Code only; Copilot needs skills invoked by name
Per-skill npx install omits the shared references/ checklists (issue #361)
Cursor and Windsurf need manual copying into rules or skills directories
Testing reference examples target JavaScript/TypeScript

projects.name: claude-mem
projects.tagline: Persistent cross-session memory plugin for Claude Code and other coding agents
projects.summary: Claude-Mem hooks into Claude Code session lifecycle events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd), records tool-usage observations and summaries in SQLite, and injects relevant context into later sessions. A local Bun-managed worker serves an HTTP API and web viewer, with hybrid FTS5 and Chroma vector search exposed through three MCP tools: search, timeline and get_observations. Installers also cover OpenCode, T3 Code, Antigravity, OMP, Pi and OpenClaw.
strengths: Search, timeline, get_observations flow filters before fetching details; README claims ~10x token savings
Local SQLite storage with FTS5 plus Chroma hybrid search, and a web viewer for stored memory
One npx installer targets Claude Code, OpenCode, T3 Code, Antigravity, OMP, Pi and others
`<private>` tags exclude content from storage; settings live in ~/.claude-mem/settings.json
weaknesses: Default installer prompts for sign-in to a hosted observer with a 30-day trial, then paid
Needs Node 20+, Bun and uv; the last two are auto-installed
`npm install -g claude-mem` installs only the SDK, not the hooks or worker
Summaries are generated by an extra model (hosted, OpenRouter, Gemini or Anthropic plan), adding usage

projects.name: impeccable
projects.tagline: Design skill with 24 commands and a detector for AI-generated frontends
projects.summary: Impeccable installs a single /impeccable skill into AI coding tools, with 24 commands such as audit, critique, polish, typeset and live browser variant iteration. It writes PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md for project context, and ships 59 deterministic detector rules that run in a CLI and browser extension without an LLM or API key. Hooks flag common AI design tells on UI file edits in supported harnesses.
strengths: Supports many harnesses: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Grok Build, Hermes
59 deterministic detector rules run without an LLM or API key
Edit hooks surface design findings; Cursor blocks bad writes before they land
Several install paths: npx installer, Git submodule, plugin marketplace, manual copy
weaknesses: Native edit hooks are not available on every harness; Hermes and Veto get none
Roll API at impeccable.style is called when a new design starts; telemetry is opt-out
Downloads an engine binary into ~/.impeccable/bin/ on first run if not bundled
Codex and Grok Build need manual hook or folder trust approval after install

projects.name: graphify
projects.tagline: Skill that maps a codebase and docs into a queryable knowledge graph
projects.summary: Graphify installs as a skill for AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI. Running /graphify parses code with tree-sitter across about 40 languages, and handles docs, PDFs, images and video through the assistant's model. It writes graph.json, graph.html and GRAPH_REPORT.md, and the graph can then be queried with query, path and explain commands instead of grepping files.
strengths: Code parsing is local tree-sitter AST, with no LLM calls and no data leaving the machine
Each edge is tagged EXTRACTED or INFERRED, so direct reads are separable from resolved links
Installs into 20+ assistants with one command per platform, including project-scoped installs
Outputs plain files (graph.json, graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md) queryable without re-reading source
weaknesses: Docs, PDFs, images and video need an LLM backend or the assistant's model for the semantic pass
PDF, Office, video, MCP and Neo4j support are separate optional extras to install
Monorepo and cross-repo support, formal verification and Sentry/Jira connectors are in paid Graphify Cloud
Benchmarks are the project's own; LOCOMO QA accuracy is below supermemory (45.3% vs 49.7%)

projects.name: archify
projects.tagline: Agent skill that turns descriptions or repos into interactive HTML diagrams
projects.summary: Archify is a skill for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, installed with `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g`. Given a description or a repository, the agent generates a self-contained interactive HTML diagram of one of five types: architecture, workflow, sequence, data flow or lifecycle. Output supports theme switching, route and reach tracing, and PNG or share-card export.
strengths: Output is standalone HTML that opens in a browser without installing Archify
Five diagram types, plus Before/Delta/After architecture comparison with a machine receipt
Works from a plain description; no repository required
Update check can be disabled with ARCHIFY_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=1 and never auto-installs
weaknesses: Needs an AI coding agent and its model; Archify does not generate diagrams alone
Optional update check makes a network GET to a fixed manifest by default
Deployment-ownership profile checks authored facts only, not live infrastructure
README is heavy on sponsors and promotion, which buries technical details

projects.name: ruflo
projects.tagline: Agent harness for Claude Code and Codex with swarms, memory and MCP tools
projects.summary: Ruflo wraps Claude Code and Codex with a CLI, an MCP server and Claude Code plugins that add agent definitions, swarm coordination, vector-backed memory, hooks and a console UI. It installs either as marketplace plugins (35 listed) or through `npx ruflo init`, which writes .claude/ config, hooks and a daemon into the project. The README cites 98 agents, 60+ commands, 30 skills and 314 MCP tools.
strengths: Two install paths: zero-file Claude Code plugins or full CLI init with hooks and MCP server
Works with any MCP client via `npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start`
Console permission levels (read/write/manage/full) with ask or auto approval
Optional standalone terminal UI via `npx ruflo tui`, with a plain mode for scripts
weaknesses: Large surface (314 MCP tools, 35 plugins) that the README itself says not to learn
Mods run with account permissions, are not sandboxed; README says read code first
Console, mods and hooks are Claude Code integrations; other clients get MCP tools only
Plugin path has different tool names and fewer features than the CLI path

projects.name: oh-my-claudecode
projects.tagline: Multi-agent orchestration plugin for Claude Code with staged team pipelines
projects.summary: oh-my-claudecode adds skills, slash commands and an `omc` CLI to Claude Code. It runs in-session workflows such as /autopilot, /ralph, /deep-interview and a staged /team pipeline (plan, PRD, exec, verify, fix). The CLI can also start tmux panes running Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Grok, Cursor or Claude workers.
strengths: Installs as a Claude Code marketplace plugin or via npm (`oh-my-claude-sisyphus`)
`omc team` spawns tmux workers for Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Grok, Cursor and Claude
Autopilot stage profiles are configurable in `.claude/omc.jsonc`
MIT license; exports TypeScript helpers such as `createOmcSession()`
weaknesses: Slash-command workflows need an active Claude Code session; not usable in CI
Named autopilot profiles require Linux with `flock`
Native team mode needs an experimental Claude Code env flag
npm install prints a deprecated `prebuild-install` warning

projects.name: cc-switch
projects.tagline: Desktop app that switches API providers for coding agents and manages their MCP and skills
projects.summary: CC Switch is a Tauri 2 desktop app written in Rust for Windows, macOS and Linux. It switches API providers for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi and MiniMax Code. It also manages MCP servers, Skills and Prompts in one place, so JSON, TOML and YAML configs need no hand-editing.
strengths: Covers ten coding agents and CLIs from one provider switcher
Manages MCP servers, Skills and Prompts alongside provider settings
Native desktop builds for Windows, macOS and Linux via Tauri 2
MIT license, with a user manual and translated READMEs
weaknesses: README opens with a long list of API relay sponsors and referral links
Desktop GUI only; no Docker image or headless mode detected
Part of the README was truncated, so install and feature details are unverified
System requirements such as minimum RAM are unknown

projects.name: gstack
projects.tagline: Slash-command skill pack giving Claude Code review, QA and ship roles
projects.summary: gstack is a set of Markdown skills, invoked as slash commands such as /office-hours, /plan-eng-review, /review, /qa, /cso and /ship, that give Claude Code defined roles for planning, code review, browser QA, security audit and release. A Bun-based ./setup installs it into ~/.claude/skills and builds a bundled browser. Experimental installs exist for Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot CLI and others.
strengths: Covers planning, review, QA, security audit and release as separate slash commands
Team mode auto-updates for shared repos without vendoring files into them
Installs on Claude Code plus experimental hosts such as Codex, Cursor and OpenCode
Setup took 31 seconds on a 4-vCPU Linux machine, per the README
weaknesses: Safety hooks like /careful and /freeze are enforced only on Claude Code
Only Claude Code is certified; other agents are experimental or instruction-only
/cso needs a recent Bun with specific build flags and a native C toolchain
Outside reviews need a signed-in Codex CLI; design tools use an OpenAI key

projects.name: rtk
projects.tagline: CLI proxy that compresses shell command output before coding agents read it
projects.summary: rtk is a single Rust binary that wraps 100+ shell commands (git, cargo test, pytest, docker, kubectl, aws and others) and returns grouped, truncated or deduplicated output. `rtk init` installs a hook for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf and other agents that rewrites Bash calls such as `git status` to `rtk git status`. The README claims up to 90% less bash output and under 10ms overhead.
strengths: Single Rust binary; README states under 10ms overhead per command
Auto-rewrite hook covers many agents: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline
Per-command filters for tests, linters, git, docker, kubectl, AWS and Pulumi
`rtk gain` reports savings history; `rtk discover` finds missed rewrites
weaknesses: Hook only affects Bash calls; Claude's built-in Read, Grep and Glob bypass it
Token counts are estimated as bytes/4; no tokenizer, so absolute numbers are approximate
Up to 90% applies to bash output only, not to the total bill
Another 'rtk' crate exists on crates.io; install via git, not the crate name

projects.name: openspec
projects.tagline: Spec-driven workflow CLI that guides AI coding assistants through plan, apply and archive
projects.summary: OpenSpec is a Node.js CLI that adds an `openspec/` folder to a repo and installs slash commands (such as /opsx:propose, /opsx:apply, /opsx:archive) into 30+ AI coding tools. Each change gets a folder with proposal.md, specs, design.md and tasks.md in plain Markdown, which the human reviews before code is written. A beta Stores feature keeps specs and changes in a separate shared repo for cross-repo work.
strengths: Specs and changes are plain Markdown in the repo, versioned with git
Works with 30+ AI coding tools through generated slash commands
Install via npm or Homebrew; no server or database needed
Designed for existing codebases, with an adoption guide for brownfield projects
weaknesses: Needs Node.js 20.19.0 or higher
Stores (cross-repo shared planning) are still in beta
Collects anonymous usage telemetry by default; opt-out via config or env var
Command syntax differs per tool, e.g. /opsx-propose, @opsx-propose, $openspec-propose

projects.name: agentic-awesome-skills
projects.tagline: Library of 2,671+ SKILL.md playbooks for coding agents, with a local MCP selector
projects.summary: A repository of installable SKILL.md instruction files for coding agents, plus AAS Core, a local MCP and `aas` CLI that lets Codex or Claude search the catalog, record chosen skills in aas-stack.json, and preview a plan. A separate npm installer copies selected skills into host directories for Cursor, Gemini CLI, Kiro, OpenCode and others. Core does not rank or recommend skills, and apply and recovery are experimental.
strengths: 2,671+ skills, searchable via skills_index.json and a hosted catalog
Installer targets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Kiro, OpenCode and Copilot
Installer supports --dry-run and filters by skill ID, category, tags and risk
MIT license; Core stack validate and plan preview are read-only
weaknesses: Core apply and recovery are experimental; supported preview stops at plan review
Core setup guides cover only Codex and Claude; other hosts use direct install
Too many installed skills can overload Antigravity's context
Validation checks structure only, not whether a skill fits or is safe

projects.name: book-to-skill
projects.tagline: Converts books and document folders into on-demand skills for coding agents
projects.summary: A Python extractor turns PDF, EPUB, DOCX, Markdown, HTML, RTF or MOBI files into clean text, and the host agent follows SKILL.md to generate a skill. The output is a core SKILL.md, per-chapter files, a glossary, patterns and a cheatsheet, written to ~/.agents/skills/<slug>/. Works with hosts that read the Agent Skills format, including Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp, Hermes Agent, OpenCode and OpenClaw.
strengths: Chapter files load on demand; SKILL.md is about 4,000 tokens
Reads PDF, EPUB, DOCX, HTML, RTF, MOBI, Markdown and plain text
One skill folder is discovered by several agent hosts
Reports 24x-51x fewer tokens than putting the book in context
weaknesses: Scanned PDFs need OCR first (e.g. ocrmypdf); extraction stops otherwise
MOBI/AZW input requires Calibre's ebook-convert, installed separately
Skill generation is done by the host agent's model, so quality varies
Sharing skills made from copyrighted books may infringe the rights holder

projects.name: taste-skill
projects.tagline: Agent Skills that steer AI coding agents toward better frontend design
projects.summary: A set of SKILL.md files that give coding agents rules for layout, typography, motion and spacing, plus image-generation skills for web, mobile and brand-kit reference boards. The default skill exposes three 1-10 dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE, MOTION_INTENSITY, VISUAL_DENSITY). Installs with `npx skills add` or as a Claude Code plugin; also usable in Codex and Cursor.
strengths: Installs per skill via `npx skills add --skill <name>` or as a Claude Code plugin
Three adjustable dials in the default skill: variance, motion intensity, visual density
Separate skills for redesign, minimalist, brutalist, soft UI and image-to-code workflows
Framework agnostic; rules target design intent rather than one framework API
weaknesses: Default taste-skill v2 is marked experimental and not yet at a stable 2.0.0
Image-generation skills need a separate generator such as ChatGPT Images
No published releases; output quality depends on the agent and model used
README gives no benchmarks or measured results, only one example screenshot

projects.name: repomix
projects.tagline: CLI that packs a repository into one file for LLM context
projects.summary: Repomix reads a local or remote Git repository and writes a single file, XML by default or Markdown, JSON or plain text, with a directory tree and file contents. It reports token counts, respects .gitignore, .ignore and .repomixignore, and uses Secretlint to leave out files matching known credential formats. The --compress option uses Tree-sitter to keep code structure while cutting tokens.
strengths: One command (npx repomix@latest) produces the packed file with no install
Token counts per file and for the whole repo help fit context limits
--compress uses Tree-sitter to reduce tokens while keeping code structure
Packs remote repos by URL, branch or commit, and file lists piped via --stdin
weaknesses: Output is a static snapshot; you paste or upload it to the model yourself
Secret detection only covers known credential formats via Secretlint
VSCode extension is community-maintained, not part of the core project
Whole large repos can exceed model context unless filtered or compressed

projects.name: claude-hud
projects.tagline: Status line plugin for Claude Code showing context, usage limits and todos
projects.summary: Claude HUD is a Claude Code plugin that registers a status line command, which prints context-window usage, subscriber rate limits, model, project path and git branch below the input. Optional lines show active tools, subagents, skills, MCP servers and todo progress, read from the session transcript. Settings live in a JSON config file or the /claude-hud:configure flow, and it needs no tmux or separate window.
strengths: Installs from the Claude Code plugin marketplace with a few slash commands
Reads session data Claude Code passes on stdin; no separate window or tmux
Extensive config: layout, element order, thresholds, colors, git and jj status
Labels available in English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese
weaknesses: Works only with Claude Code
Subscriber usage limits are hidden on API-key, Bedrock and Vertex sessions
Tools, agents and todos lines are off by default and parse the transcript
Needs a JavaScript runtime; Windows users must install Node.js separately

projects.name: agents
projects.tagline: Plugin, agent and skill collection for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and others
projects.summary: A catalog of 94 plugins (92 local, 2 external) holding 202 agents, 184 skills and 105 commands, written once as Markdown in the Claude Code plugin format. Native marketplaces serve Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor, while adapters generate artifacts for OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot and Pi. Individual skills can be installed alone with `gh skill` or `npx skills`.
strengths: One Markdown source adapted to seven coding tools
Skills install individually via gh skill or npx skills
Broad coverage: Python, JavaScript, testing, security, infrastructure
MIT license; plugin-eval runs static skill checks without model calls
weaknesses: OpenCode, Antigravity, Copilot and Pi need a clone, uv and Python 3.12+
Features differ by harness; Codex agents and commands use a separate generated path
Pi agents need a subagent extension
plugin-eval LLM judge and Monte Carlo layers are experimental, not validated against human labels

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: CLI that installs SKILL.md agent skills into dozens of coding agents
projects.summary: An npm CLI (`npx skills`) that fetches skills defined as SKILL.md files from GitHub, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL, a local path or an archive URL, and installs them into each coding agent's skills directory. It supports project or global scope and symlinked or copied installs, and it adds list, find, update, remove and init commands. The README lists about 80 supported agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
strengths: One command installs a skill into many agents' directories, using symlinks to a canonical copy
Accepts GitHub shorthand, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL, local paths and archive URLs
Private repos use existing Git credentials, GitHub CLI or SSH; a token is optional
Non-interactive flags (-y, --all, -g, -a) make it usable in CI
weaknesses: Needs Node.js and npx; the README does not state a minimum version
Only manages skills; it does not supply the agents themselves
Agent support depends on a hand-maintained table of paths for each agent
Symlinks may not work on every platform; copy mode is the fallback

projects.name: planning-with-files
projects.tagline: Agent skill that keeps task plans in markdown files that survive /clear
projects.summary: Keeps task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md in the project and uses lifecycle hooks to re-inject the active plan each turn, so a coding agent resumes after /clear, compaction or a crash. A Stop-time completion gate can hold the agent until the plan reports complete. Installs via `npx skills add` for 60+ agents, with native plugins for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Qoder CLI, Pi, Hermes, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness.
strengths: Plain markdown plan files on disk, no runtime state or database elsewhere
Native plugins for several hosts plus the generic Agent Skills install route
Completion gate holds the agent's stop until the plan reports complete
Translated variants in 5 languages ship the full script surface
weaknesses: Hook behavior and available commands differ per host; Qoder CLI needs Bash and Python 3.10+
Plan files are gitignored and overwritten by the next task unless you keep them
Benchmark claims rest on small samples (3 blind A/B comparisons, 30 assertions)
Completion gate depends on literal English status tokens matched with grep -F

projects.name: agency-agents
projects.tagline: Markdown agent persona files for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding tools
projects.summary: A repository of role-specific agent definitions written as Markdown files and grouped into divisions such as engineering and design. Each file describes the agent's identity, workflow, code examples and success metrics. Shell scripts (convert.sh, install.sh) generate and install the files for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Aider, Windsurf, Codex and others. A separate desktop app for macOS, Linux and Windows does the same install with a GUI.
strengths: Installs into 14+ tools via one script, with --division and --agent filters
Roster spans dozens of engineering roles, from SRE and RAG pipelines to Solidity
Plain Markdown files, easy to read, copy and adapt without running anything
Separate desktop app handles install and updates without a clone
weaknesses: Prompt files only; no runtime, orchestration or agent execution included
OpenCode registers only about 119 agents, so full installs get silently truncated
No tagged release; versioning relies on commit history
Effectiveness claims like 'battle-tested' are not backed by benchmarks in the README

projects.name: beads
projects.tagline: Dependency-aware issue tracker CLI that gives coding agents persistent task memory
projects.summary: bd (Beads) is a Go CLI that stores tasks as a dependency graph in a Dolt database, replacing markdown TODO lists for coding agents. Agents use commands such as bd ready, bd update --claim and bd close, with JSON output and hash-based IDs to avoid merge collisions. bd setup installs hooks and instructions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others; sync runs through Dolt remotes on a git remote.
strengths: Hash-based IDs (bd-a1b2) avoid merge collisions across agents and branches
Embedded Dolt mode needs no separate database server
bd setup installs integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Factory and more
Works without git via BEADS_DIR and --stealth, including non-git VCS
weaknesses: Embedded mode is single-writer; concurrent writers need an external dolt sql-server
HTTP backend is marked experimental and diverges from local behavior in documented ways
Upgrades across schema migrations need a designated clone to migrate and push
issues.jsonl is only an export, not a backup; sync relies on Dolt remotes

projects.name: understand-anything
projects.tagline: Plugin that builds an explorable knowledge graph of a codebase or wiki
projects.summary: Understand Anything is a plugin for Claude Code and about 15 other agent platforms. Its /understand command runs a multi-agent pipeline that combines Tree-sitter parsing with LLM summaries to write a knowledge graph to .ua/knowledge-graph.json. A local dashboard then offers graph navigation, search, guided tours, diff impact analysis and chat, and /understand-knowledge handles Karpathy-style LLM wikis.
strengths: Tree-sitter extracts imports and call sites deterministically, so structural edges are reproducible
Graph is plain JSON that can be committed; teammates view it with Node.js >= 18 and no LLM
Incremental re-analysis of changed files, plus an optional post-commit auto-update hook
Installs on Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro and others
weaknesses: First /understand run on a large repo can use a significant number of tokens
Needs a host agent platform and an LLM; it is not a standalone tool
Output languages limited to en, zh, zh-TW, ja, ko, ru, vi
Graphs over 10 MB need git-lfs to commit comfortably

projects.name: claude-code-best-practice
projects.tagline: Reference repo of Claude Code configs, guides, and workflow examples
projects.summary: A documentation-first repository that catalogs Claude Code features (subagents, commands, skills, hooks, MCP servers, settings, memory, plugins) with written guidance and working examples under `.claude/`. It includes a Command → Agent → Skill orchestration demo run with `/weather-orchestrator`, plus a comparison table of community development workflows such as Superpowers, Spec Kit and gstack.
strengths: Each feature links to both a written guide and a working implementation in the repo
Runnable orchestration example: Command → Agent → Skill via `/weather-orchestrator`
Compares community workflows with agent, command and skill counts per project
MIT license; plain markdown and config files, no services to run
weaknesses: Covers Claude Code only; other coding agents are not the focus
Not installable software; it is reference material to read and copy from
Many listed features are marked beta and may change
Workflow table figures such as star counts are snapshots that go stale

projects.name: claude-howto
projects.tagline: Tutorials and copy-paste templates for Claude Code features
projects.summary: A Markdown guide with 10 modules covering Claude Code slash commands, memory, skills, subagents, MCP, hooks, plugins, checkpoints, advanced features and the CLI. Each module ships templates to copy into .claude/ or ~/.claude/, plus Mermaid diagrams. The README estimates 11-13 hours for the full path and includes quiz commands, /self-assessment and /lesson-quiz.
strengths: Templates copy directly into .claude/commands, .claude/agents and ~/.claude/skills
Ordered learning path with per-module time estimates
MIT licensed; README says it is synced with Claude Code releases
Covers hooks, MCP, subagents and plugins in one place
weaknesses: Documentation and templates only; no runnable application or service
Tied to Claude Code; templates are not portable to other coding agents
Docker support and a hosted demo are not provided
README leans on promotional claims such as 10x productivity, unsupported by evidence

projects.name: i-have-adhd
projects.tagline: Skill that makes coding assistants answer with the next action first
projects.summary: A skill/plugin for coding assistants that rewrites response style around ten rules: lead with the next action, number multi-step tasks, cap lists at 5 items, and drop preambles, recaps and closers. It installs through Claude's plugin commands and is tuned by editing skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md in a fork. The README's before/after example turns a long auth-flow explanation into three numbered steps.
strengths: Ten explicit rules, documented in a single editable SKILL.md
Fork-and-swap workflow documented with Claude plugin commands
Before/after example shows the exact change in output style
MIT license; README translated into nine other languages
weaknesses: Install and tuning steps are documented only for Claude plugin commands
No tagged releases
Changes response style only; no measured effect on answer quality is given
Hard rules like the 5-item list cap may cut detail you need

projects.name: claude-code-templates
projects.tagline: Installable agents, commands, hooks and MCP configs for Claude Code
projects.summary: A catalog of Claude Code components (agents, slash commands, settings, hooks, MCP integrations and skills) installed per item with `npx claude-code-templates@latest` and browsable at aitmpl.com. It also ships npx-run tools: an analytics view for Claude Code sessions, a mobile-friendly conversation monitor with optional Cloudflare Tunnel access, a health check and a plugin dashboard.
strengths: One npx command installs a chosen agent, command, hook, setting, skill or MCP
Web catalog at aitmpl.com plus docs at docs.aitmpl.com
Includes analytics, health-check and conversation-monitor tools beyond the templates
MIT license; bundled third-party components keep their original licenses
weaknesses: Targets Claude Code only; no other coding assistant is mentioned
Many components come from third-party repos under mixed licenses (MIT, CC0, Apache 2.0)
README gives no per-component quality or review process; vetting is left to the user
Requires Node.js for npx; version requirements are unknown

projects.name: diagram-design
projects.tagline: Agent skill that generates editorial HTML/SVG diagrams in your site's style
projects.summary: Diagram Design is an Agent Skill, installable as a plugin for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid and Pi, that generates diagrams as self-contained HTML and SVG with no build step or JavaScript. It covers more than 40 diagram types, each in minimal light, minimal dark and full-editorial variants, and can match your brand by reading your website. It can also redraw draw.io, Mermaid or Excalidraw sources.
strengths: Output is static HTML and SVG, openable in a browser with no build step
Over 40 diagram types, each with light, dark and full-editorial variants
Installs through marketplaces for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Droid and Pi
Imports Mermaid and Excalidraw sources, with export and doctor commands
weaknesses: Needs an Agent Skills-compatible host; no standalone app or CLI generator
Attribute-only comparisons are not drawn; the README says to use tables
Standalone `npx skills` install does not auto-update and omits the command surfaces
OpenCode has no marketplace package; updates mean replacing the copied directory

projects.name: claude-skills
projects.tagline: Skills and plugins library for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor
projects.summary: A collection of SKILL.md instruction packages, stdlib-only Python CLI scripts and reference docs across 20 domains, including engineering, marketing, compliance, C-level advisory and research. It installs as Claude Code plugins from a marketplace, or converts with scripts/convert.sh into Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode and Augment formats. Personas and agent definitions are included.
strengths: Python tools are stdlib-only, no pip installs required
Installs via Claude Code plugin marketplace, per domain or per skill
convert.sh and install.sh target Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Augment
Includes a skill-security-auditor to scan skills before installation
weaknesses: Broad scope; many domains are non-coding (marketing, finance, compliance)
README counts are inconsistent (345 vs 388 skills, 5,200+ stars claim)
Hermes Agent and Mistral Vibe need a manual one-time sync script
Windows needs a symlink-enabled clone and PYTHONUTF8=1 for mirror trees

projects.name: claude-code-game-studios
projects.tagline: Claude Code template with 49 game-studio subagents, 74 slash-command skills and hooks
projects.summary: A project template that adds studio-style structure to Claude Code for game development: 49 subagents in three tiers, 74 skills such as /start, /brainstorm and /dev-story, 12 hooks and 13 path-scoped rules. A project.yaml `modes.rigor` setting (minimal, standard, full) controls how much documentation and review the workflow requires. It includes agent sets for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal Engine 5.
strengths: Engine-specific agent sets for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal Engine 5
Single modes.rigor setting scales process from jam-style minimal to full director review
Hooks validate commits, pushes and asset JSON; deny rules block force push and rm -rf
Stories that change visuals need a launched game and a retained screenshot to close
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code; no other coding agent is mentioned
Hooks need Bash, and Python 3 is needed to read project.yaml
README's own test ranked the standard rigor build last against minimal
No sample game is shipped, so output quality cannot be inspected in the repo

projects.name: claude-plugins-official
projects.tagline: Anthropic's curated plugin marketplace for Claude Code
projects.summary: A Git repository that acts as the official plugin marketplace for Claude Code. Plugins install with `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official` or through `/plugin > Discover`. The repo holds Anthropic-maintained plugins in `/plugins` and partner or community plugins in `/external_plugins`, each bundling any of MCP server config, slash commands, agents and skills.
strengths: Installs directly from inside Claude Code with one slash command
Documents a standard plugin layout with an example plugin as reference
Plugin names are immutable slugs, with a renames map for migrations
Supports skill-bundle entries for repos that ship SKILL.md files without a manifest
weaknesses: Only useful with Claude Code; not a standalone tool
Anthropic does not control or verify third-party plugin contents, which can change
No single license; each plugin carries its own LICENSE file
No tagged releases; plugins are pinned only by marketplace entry

projects.name: agentskills
projects.tagline: Open specification for SKILL.md folders that give AI agents reusable instructions
projects.summary: Defines the Agent Skills format: a folder with a SKILL.md file holding name and description metadata plus instructions, and optional scripts, references and assets. Agents load skills in three stages (discovery, activation, execution), so only names and descriptions sit in context until a task matches. Originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard; the repo holds the spec and docs, not a runtime.
strengths: Minimal format: one SKILL.md with name and description is enough
Progressive disclosure keeps context small with many skills installed
Skills can bundle scripts, references and templates in one version-controlled folder
Supported by multiple agent clients, listed in a client showcase
weaknesses: Specification and docs only; it is not an agent or runtime
Behavior depends on how each client implements skill loading
No tagged releases; versioning of the spec is not stated in the README
Skill quality and security of bundled scripts are left to authors

projects.name: design.md
projects.tagline: Spec and CLI for describing a design system to coding agents
projects.summary: DESIGN.md defines a file format with YAML front matter for design tokens (colors, typography, rounded, spacing, components) and markdown prose for rationale. The TypeScript CLI, run with npx, lints files for broken token references and WCAG contrast, diffs two versions, and exports tokens to Tailwind v3/v4 and W3C DTCG. The format is at version alpha.
strengths: Lint output is structured JSON with a non-zero exit code on errors, usable in CI
Eleven lint rules cover broken refs, WCAG AA contrast, section order and typos
Exports to Tailwind v3 JSON, Tailwind v4 CSS @theme and W3C DTCG tokens
Also usable as a library via the @google/design.md/linter import
weaknesses: Format is marked alpha; the README warns the spec and schema will change
Only a fixed set of component properties is valid; others produce warnings
Sections must appear in a fixed order, otherwise the linter warns
Windows needs the designmd alias because of the .md bin name collision

projects.name: hallmark
projects.tagline: Design skill that steers coding agents away from generic AI-looking UI
projects.summary: Hallmark is a skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that picks a page macrostructure for a brief, applies one of twenty-one themes, and runs fifty-seven slop-test gates plus a self-critique before returning output. It has four verbs: build (default), audit, redesign and study, which extracts design traits from a screenshot or URL. Output is self-contained HTML and CSS.
strengths: Works across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex from one SKILL.md plus references
Audit verb scores existing code and returns a punch list without editing
Twenty-one themes plus a Custom branch for briefs no theme fits
Live demo site and example pages are linked for each theme
weaknesses: Example output is static HTML and CSS; framework support is not documented
Cursor install needs manual copy into a .mdc rule without frontmatter
No benchmarks showing the slop-test gates improve output
No tagged releases

projects.name: security-audit-skill
projects.tagline: Coding-agent skill that runs a multi-phase security audit of a codebase
projects.summary: A skill for coding agents that audits a repository for vulnerabilities in six phases: reconnaissance, hunting, candidate validation, structured output, record verification and reporting. Isolated sub-agents hunt from a coverage ledger, and a fresh agent tries to disprove each candidate. Results go to findings.json, checked by Node validators, and to REPORT.md. It is the single-repo starting point for Cloudflare's vulnerability harness.
strengths: Separate agents find and validate each finding; verdicts are confirmed, needs_validation or rejected
Zero-dependency Node validators check findings.json and coverage-ledger.json against a schema
Attack-class prompts cover memory safety, web/auth, cloud, supply chain, client-side and LLM targets
Repeated runs reuse prior ledgers and findings to target coverage gaps
weaknesses: Needs a model with tool use and parallel sub-agents; token cost is unknown
Running target code requires an OS-enforced sandbox you must provide, else leads stay unvalidated
README says a single run found roughly half of what repeated runs found
No release published; install goes through the Skills CLI via npx

projects.name: codex-plugin-cc
projects.tagline: Claude Code plugin that runs Codex reviews and delegates tasks
projects.summary: A Claude Code plugin that adds slash commands for running Codex code reviews and handing tasks to Codex without leaving Claude Code. It wraps the local Codex CLI and app server, so it reuses your existing Codex login, config.toml and base URL settings. Background jobs can be tracked and cancelled, and sessions can be resumed in Codex.
strengths: Reuses local Codex CLI auth and config.toml; no separate runtime
Read-only /codex:review and steerable /codex:adversarial-review with --base <ref>
Background jobs via /codex:status, /codex:result and /codex:cancel
Sessions can be continued in Codex with codex resume <session-id>
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code plus a ChatGPT subscription or OpenAI API key
Usage counts against Codex limits; optional review gate can drain them quickly
Multi-file reviews and rescue tasks can run long
/codex:transfer needs a Codex version that supports session import

projects.name: frontend-slides
projects.tagline: Claude Code skill that generates HTML slide decks or converts PowerPoint files
projects.summary: A skill for Claude Code, packaged as a plugin, that builds single-file HTML presentations with inline CSS and JS. It shows three visual style previews to pick from, then writes the full deck, or extracts text, images and notes from a .pptx and rebuilds it for the web. Other coding agents can follow the same SKILL.md if they have filesystem and shell access.
strengths: Output is one HTML file with inline CSS/JS, no npm or build step
Converts .pptx files, extracting text, images and speaker notes
Ships 12 included styles plus 34 optional bold templates loaded on demand
Installs as a Claude Code plugin or by copying files into ~/.claude/skills
weaknesses: Plugin install flow and slash command are specific to Claude Code
Other agents must read SKILL.md manually; no install path is documented for them
Output is fixed 16:9 HTML, not editable .pptx
Style previews depend on the agent's generation, so results vary per run

projects.name: codegraph
projects.tagline: Local code knowledge graph served to coding agents over MCP
projects.summary: CodeGraph indexes a project into a local graph of symbols, call edges and dependencies under `.codegraph/`, then exposes it to coding agents through an MCP server. Agents can fetch relevant source, call paths and change impact in one call instead of grepping and reading files. `codegraph install` wires it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Gemini CLI, Kiro, GitHub Copilot and others, and auto-sync keeps the index current.
strengths: Runs locally; no Node.js needed, ships as a bundled installer or npm package
One `codegraph install` configures MCP for nine named agents and IDEs
Covers 30+ languages, including TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, Swift
Watches files and updates the graph automatically; no manual re-index
weaknesses: README admits about 80% more retrieval context stays resident in long sessions
Published benchmarks are the author's, on 7 repos with one question each
No Docker or compose setup; install is via curl/PowerShell script or npm
Hosted CodeGraph platform is a waitlist product, separate from this repo

projects.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
projects.tagline: MCP server that lets coding agents drive and debug a live Chrome
projects.summary: chrome-devtools-mcp is an MCP server that gives coding agents such as Claude, Cursor and Copilot control of a live Chrome browser. It records performance traces through Chrome DevTools, inspects network requests and console messages with source-mapped stack traces, and automates page actions via puppeteer. A CLI is included for use without MCP, and a --slim mode exposes a smaller tool set.
strengths: Records DevTools performance traces and extracts insights from them
Puppeteer-based automation waits for action results automatically
Slim mode limits the exposed tools to basic browser tasks
Also ships a CLI for use without an MCP client
weaknesses: Usage statistics are sent to Google by default; opt out with --no-usage-statistics
Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API
Officially supports only Chrome and Chrome for Testing
Exposes all browser content to the connected MCP client

projects.name: codebase-memory-mcp
projects.tagline: MCP server that indexes codebases into a queryable knowledge graph
projects.summary: A native C executable that parses repositories with tree-sitter (162 languages) into a persistent graph of functions, classes, call chains, HTTP routes and cross-service links, and exposes it through 17 MCP tools. It adds semantic search with bundled embeddings, Cypher-like queries, dead code detection, git diff impact mapping and a built-in 3D graph UI. Processing is local, and `install` configures detected coding-agent clients.
strengths: Runs locally with no API key, hosted service or language runtime
Bundled embeddings enable semantic search without Ollama or Docker
Covers 162 languages; Hybrid LSP type resolution for 10 of them
Releases are VirusTotal-scanned and SLSA 3 attested
weaknesses: Updates require re-running the install script; `update` only prints the command
Defender may flag release binaries as a false positive, per the README
All active processes must share the exact same build and cache root
Watcher covers only git projects opened in MCP sessions, by default

projects.name: github-mcp-server
projects.tagline: MCP server exposing GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions to AI tools
projects.summary: Official GitHub MCP server, written in Go, that lets MCP hosts read code, manage issues and pull requests, inspect Actions runs and review security alerts. It runs either as a GitHub-hosted remote endpoint (api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/) or locally over stdio via the ghcr.io Docker image or a binary built with go build. Authentication is OAuth or a personal access token.
strengths: Hosted remote endpoint needs no local install; local Docker image and Go build also available
Supports OAuth login or PAT; PAT takes precedence when set
Works with GitHub Enterprise Cloud (ghe.com) and Enterprise Server via GITHUB_HOST
Install guides for VS Code, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Codex and others
weaknesses: Enterprise Server is not supported by the remote server; local server only
Remote OAuth needs each host to configure a GitHub App or OAuth App
Local Docker OAuth needs a fixed callback port (8085) published to loopback
Only talks to GitHub; no other forges or providers

projects.name: serena
projects.tagline: MCP server giving coding agents symbol-level code search, editing and refactoring
projects.summary: Serena is an MCP server that gives a coding agent IDE-style tools: find symbol, find references, replace symbol body, rename, and a memory system. It uses language servers (over 40 languages) by default, or a paid JetBrains plugin that adds move, inline, type hierarchy and a debugger. It plugs into MCP clients such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VSCode.
strengths: Symbol-level retrieval and editing instead of line numbers or text search
Language server backend is free and covers over 40 languages
Works with any MCP client, launched by command or run in HTTP mode
Layered YAML configuration: global, per-project, per-client contexts and modes
weaknesses: Move, inline, type hierarchy and debugging need the paid JetBrains plugin
Language server rename covers symbols only; some languages need extra installs
Application is GPL-3.0-or-later; only the SolidLSP component is MIT
Contributions require accepting a CLA

projects.name: code-review-graph
projects.tagline: Local Tree-sitter code graph served over MCP so agents read only affected files
projects.summary: Parses a repository with Tree-sitter into a SQLite graph of functions, classes, imports, calls, inheritance and tests, then serves blast-radius and review context to AI coding tools over MCP. A single install command detects and configures about 16 tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and Zed. It also ships a GitHub Action that posts risk-scored PR comments, and updates the graph incrementally by SHA-256 hash.
strengths: One install command configures about 16 coding tools; uninstall leaves other config intact
Incremental re-parse by SHA-256; two-file edit on a ~3,000-file repo took about 2.5 s
Covers 30+ languages and notebooks, plus custom languages via languages.toml
Pinned-SHA benchmarks with a reproduction recipe; median 63x token reduction across 6 repos
weaknesses: Impact recall of 1.0 is circular, since ground truth comes from the same graph
Graph context can exceed a plain file read for small single-file edits
Search ranking needs work; Express queries can return no hits
Flow detection is strongest for Python and PHP/Laravel; JavaScript and Go are weaker

projects.name: context7
projects.tagline: Fetches current, version-specific library docs into coding agent prompts
projects.summary: Context7 looks up documentation and code examples for a named library and version, then returns them to the coding agent as context. It runs as an MCP server with two tools (resolve-library-id, query-docs) or as a ctx7 CLI plus skill. Setup is one command, npx ctx7 setup, which handles OAuth and API key generation. The hosted service at mcp.context7.com does the retrieval.
strengths: Two modes: MCP server, or ctx7 CLI with an installed skill
Library IDs like /vercel/next.js skip matching; version can be named in the prompt
npx ctx7 setup configures Cursor, Claude Code or opencode
Also ships a TypeScript SDK and Vercel AI SDK tools
weaknesses: API backend, parsing and crawling engines are private; repo has only the MCP server
Relies on the hosted service at mcp.context7.com; local run is a separate guide
Free API key recommended for higher rate limits; exact limits unknown
Docs are community-contributed; accuracy and security are not guaranteed

projects.name: cli-anything
projects.tagline: Generates command-line wrappers so AI agents can drive desktop and backend software
projects.summary: CLI-Anything runs a 7-phase generator inside a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. It produces a Python (Click) CLI harness with JSON output and a SKILL.md for a target application or codebase. A companion package, cli-anything-hub, installs community-built CLIs from a registry, covering GIMP, Blender, LibreOffice, QGIS, n8n and others.
strengths: Ready-made registry of community CLIs installable with `cli-hub install <name>`
Generated CLIs emit structured JSON and ship a SKILL.md for agent discovery
Works with several agent hosts: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Pi, OpenCode
Apache-2.0 license; README reports 2,461 passing tests
weaknesses: Many CLIs only wrap an upstream app, which must be installed separately
Generating a new CLI requires a supported AI coding agent, so output quality varies
Harness quality is per-CLI and community-contributed; test depth differs between harnesses
