Prebuilt images cover CPU, NVIDIA CUDA and experimental AMD ROCm; Apple Silicon runs natively via uv.
strengths: Drop-in for the OpenAI speech API; works with the stock OpenAI Python client
Prebuilt CPU and CUDA images for amd64 and arm64 with models baked in
Voice mixing, aliases, inline speaker tags and timestamped captions
Bundled web UI at /web and Swagger docs at /docs
weaknesses: Tied to one model, Kokoro-82M; no other TTS engines
ROCm support is experimental and amd64 only
Apple Silicon GPU (MPS) needs a native uv run, not Docker
Voice tuning from a reference clip is off by default, English only, and approximate

projects.name: Pocket TTS
projects.tagline: CPU-only text-to-speech model with voice cloning and streaming
projects.summary: Pocket TTS is a 100M-parameter text-to-speech model from Kyutai that runs on CPU, using about 2 cores. It ships a Python API and a CLI with generate, serve and export-voice commands, and clones voices from a wav sample. It supports seven languages, streams audio with roughly 200ms to first chunk, and reaches about 6x real-time on a MacBook Air M4.
strengths: Runs on 2 CPU cores, no GPU required; about 6x real-time on a MacBook Air M4
Voice cloning from a wav file, with export to safetensors for fast reloads
Seven languages (en, fr, de, pt, it, es, nl) plus community models such as Czech, Hindi and Korean
Installs with pip or uvx; serve command gives a local web UI and HTTP endpoint
weaknesses: GPU use is unofficial: no device argument on load_model, and serve and Docker image are CPU-only
Cannot insert silence in the text input to create pauses
Default Linux pip install pulls CUDA PyTorch (~3 GB) unless the CPU index is passed
Pre-made voice embeddings do not work with community-trained models

projects.name: OpenReader
projects.tagline: Reads EPUB, PDF and DOCX aloud with synced word highlighting
projects.summary: Next.js server that narrates EPUB, PDF, TXT, Markdown and DOCX files with synchronized read-along, generating audio ahead of playback through a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible TTS server (Kokoro-FastAPI, KittenTTS-FastAPI, Orpheus-FastAPI) or OpenAI, Replicate and DeepInfra. PDF layout is parsed with PP-DocLayoutV3 and words aligned with ONNX Whisper in a NATS JetStream worker. Exports M4B or MP3 audiobooks.
strengths: Layout-aware PDF parsing and word-by-word highlighting
Audio cache reused across seeks, reloads and audiobook export
Storage on embedded SeaweedFS or S3; SQLite or Postgres; built-in auth
amd64 and arm64 Docker images with automatic startup migrations
weaknesses: Needs a separate TTS server or cloud TTS API; nothing is bundled
Word alignment and DOCX conversion run in a NATS JetStream compute worker you deploy
Setup details (ports, env vars) are only in the external docs

projects.name: IndexTTS
projects.tagline: Zero-shot TTS with emotion, speed and pronunciation control
projects.summary: Clones a voice from one reference clip and synthesizes speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish and Arabic (IndexTTS-2.5). Emotion comes from a second reference clip, an 8-value vector or the text itself; speed is set by duration_factor (0.5x to 2.0x) and pronunciation by inline Pinyin, CMU phonemes or Kana. Ships a Gradio web UI on port 7860 and a Python API; a vLLM recipe covers production serving.
strengths: Emotion control via reference audio, an 8-value vector or a text description
Inline pronunciation overrides: Pinyin, CMU phonemes and Japanese Kana
BF16 inference with optional DeepSpeed and compiled CUDA kernels
Published vLLM recipe for production deployment
weaknesses: No Dockerfile or compose file; install is uv plus CUDA Toolkit 12.8 or newer
Model weights (IndexTTS-2.5, IndexTTS-2) are separate multi-GB downloads
Five languages only; no streaming API is documented in the README
License is non-standard (GitHub reports NOASSERTION); check terms before commercial use

projects.name: GPT-SoVITS
projects.tagline: Few-shot voice cloning and TTS with a training web UI
projects.summary: Clones a voice from a 5-second sample (zero-shot) or fine-tunes GPT and SoVITS models on about one minute of audio, then synthesizes speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese. The Gradio web UI bundles dataset tools: UVR5 vocal separation, slicing, ASR and label proofreading. Aimed at hobbyists and studios building custom voices locally.
strengths: Zero-shot cloning from 5 s of audio; few-shot fine-tune from about 1 minute
Cross-lingual synthesis across zh, en, ja, ko and yue
Compose services for CUDA 12.6 and 12.8, plus Lite images without ASR and UVR5 models
Reported RTF 0.028 on an RTX 4060 Ti for v2 ProPlus
weaknesses: Pretrained weights are separate downloads from Hugging Face or ModelScope
Docker images lag the code; README says to pull latest source before using them
Training on Apple Silicon GPUs gives lower quality; macOS falls back to CPU
Five model generations (v1 to v5) with different tradeoffs to choose between

projects.name: vibevoice
projects.tagline: Microsoft's open speech models for long-form ASR and streaming TTS
projects.summary: VibeVoice is a family of speech models built on 7.5 Hz continuous tokenizers and next-token diffusion. The ASR models transcribe up to 60 minutes of audio in one pass with speaker, timestamp and hotword support, plus a streaming variant and a CPU build. The TTS side includes a 0.5B real-time model with about 300 ms first-audio latency. The 1.5B long-form TTS code was removed from the repository after misuse.
strengths: ASR handles 60 minutes in one pass, returning speaker, timestamps and text together
Streaming ASR, vLLM serving and ASR fine-tuning code are documented
BitNet CPU build shrinks ASR from 4.62 GB to 1.58 GB, RTF under 1 on 3+ threads
Realtime TTS is 0.5B with about 300 ms first audible latency and streaming text input
weaknesses: VibeVoice-TTS code was removed; the 1.5B TTS model is listed as Disabled
README says it is for research only, not recommended for commercial use
Realtime TTS long-form output is about 10 minutes
README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements for the full models

projects.name: F5-TTS
projects.tagline: Flow-matching TTS and voice cloning with Gradio and CLI
projects.summary: Synthesizes speech from a reference clip and its transcript using the F5-TTS diffusion transformer (plus an E2 TTS reproduction). Runs as a pip package with a Gradio web app on port 7860, a CLI and a Docker image; a Triton and TensorRT-LLM runtime reaches RTF 0.039 on an L20 GPU. Suited to researchers and builders who want a trainable open TTS model.
strengths: pip install f5-tts; Gradio UI, CLI and a ghcr.io Docker image
Triton plus TensorRT-LLM runtime: 253 ms average latency at concurrency 2 on L20
Training and fine-tuning via Accelerate or a Gradio finetune app
PyTorch install documented for NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, Intel XPU and Apple Silicon
weaknesses: Pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC (Emilia data); code is MIT, models are non-commercial
Reference audio needs a transcript, or an ASR model runs and uses more GPU memory
No compose file in the repo; the README's compose example assumes an NVIDIA GPU
Base checkpoints cover Chinese and English; other languages need community models

projects.name: Speakr
projects.tagline: Self-hosted audio transcription with speaker labels, summaries and chat over recordings
projects.summary: Speakr is a Flask and Vue web app that records or imports audio, transcribes it through a configurable engine (WhisperX, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral, AssemblyAI and others), and generates summaries, titles and action items. It adds per-recording chat, semantic search across the library, tags with custom prompts, groups, OIDC SSO, a REST API and signed webhooks. Storage is SQLite by default or PostgreSQL.
strengths: Many ASR connectors, auto-detected from config, including fully self-hosted WhisperX and VibeVoice
Speaker diarization and cross-recording voice profiles with the WhisperX backend
Multi-user with OIDC SSO, groups, sharing, retention policies and per-user usage budgets
REST API with Swagger UI and HMAC-signed webhooks for n8n, Zapier or Make
weaknesses: Voice profiles and WhisperX diarization need a separate ASR container with a GPU
Version is 0.10.14-alpha; the release is labeled alpha
Summaries and chat need an external LLM API key, or a local model such as Ollama
Full image is about 4.4GB; lite image falls back to basic text search

projects.name: whisper
projects.tagline: Multilingual speech recognition and translation model with Python and CLI interfaces
projects.summary: Whisper is a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model for speech recognition, speech-to-English translation, and language identification. It ships as a pip package with a `whisper` command and a Python API, in six sizes from tiny (39M parameters) to large (1550M), plus a turbo variant. Code and weights are MIT licensed.
strengths: Six model sizes (39M to 1550M parameters) trade accuracy for speed and VRAM
Handles transcription, translation to English and language identification in one model
Simple `whisper audio.mp3 --model turbo` CLI and a short Python API
Code and weights both under MIT license
weaknesses: No built-in HTTP server or web UI; you wrap it yourself
The turbo model is not trained for translation and returns the original language
Requires ffmpeg, and possibly Rust for tiktoken if no prebuilt wheel exists
Accuracy varies widely by language; large model needs about 10 GB VRAM

projects.name: WhisperLive
projects.tagline: Near-real-time Whisper transcription server over WebSocket
projects.summary: Streams audio from a microphone, file, RTSP or HLS source to a server on port 9090 and returns partial and committed Whisper transcripts over WebSocket, with an optional OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint. Backends are faster-whisper (CPU, CUDA, ROCm), TensorRT-LLM and OpenVINO; extras include word timestamps, hotwords, pyannote diarization and translation. For teams embedding live captions or dictation.
strengths: Three inference backends: faster-whisper, TensorRT-LLM, OpenVINO (Intel iGPU/dGPU)
Prebuilt GPU, CPU and OpenVINO Docker images; ROCm Dockerfile
Word-level timestamps, hotword boosting and batched multi-client inference
Chrome, Firefox and iOS clients; Python streaming client for raw PCM
weaknesses: Defaults allow 4 clients and 600 s per connection; must be tuned for more
Without a fixed model, a new Whisper instance loads per client connection
TensorRT backend requires building engines and is recommended only via Docker
Diarization needs the optional pyannote.audio dependency

projects.name: chattts
projects.tagline: Text-to-speech model for dialogue, with laughter and pause control
projects.summary: ChatTTS is a Python text-to-speech model trained for conversational speech in English and Chinese, with multi-speaker support and token-level control over laughter, pauses and interjections. It installs from PyPI, outputs 24 kHz audio, and ships a simple WebUI and command-line example. The released weights are a 40,000-hour pretrained model without SFT, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 for research use.
strengths: Token-level prosody control: [laugh], [uv_break], [lbreak], plus sentence-level oral/laugh/break prompts
Random speaker sampling with saved embeddings for timbre recovery
Streaming generation and zero-shot inference code are included
Runs with about 4 GB GPU memory for a 30-second clip; RTF around 0.3 on a 4090
weaknesses: Model weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, academic use only; no commercial use
Only English and Chinese supported; English is described as experimental
Autoregressive output is unstable: speaker drift and quality vary between samples
Repo is the algorithm and examples; no packaged server or Docker image

projects.name: Speaches
projects.tagline: OpenAI-compatible STT and TTS server with faster-whisper, Kokoro and Piper
projects.summary: Exposes OpenAI-style audio endpoints: streaming transcription and translation through faster-whisper, speech generation through Kokoro and Piper, plus a Realtime API and audio chat completions. Models load on first request and unload after inactivity, on CPU or GPU, via Docker Compose. For self-hosters who want one container that OpenAI SDKs can talk to for speech.
strengths: Works with any OpenAI SDK; transcription streams over SSE
Dynamic model loading and unloading after idle time
Supports the Realtime API and audio-in, audio-out chat completions
CPU and GPU Docker images with Compose files
weaknesses: Last commit April 2026; development has slowed
README is short; port, env vars and limits live only in the external docs
TTS limited to Kokoro and Piper models
Streaming transcription demo is marked TODO in the README

projects.name: ComfyUI
projects.tagline: Node-graph engine for diffusion image, video, audio and 3D models
projects.summary: Builds generation pipelines as a visual node graph and runs them locally for image (SD 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux.1 and Flux.2, Qwen Image), video (Wan 2.x, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo), audio (ACE-Step, Stable Audio) and 3D (Hunyuan3D) models, with a local API and an App Mode that exposes a workflow as a simple UI. Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon and Ascend. For professionals who want control over every parameter.
strengths: Asynchronous weight streaming runs large models on 4 GB VRAM plus 8 GB RAM
Workflows saved as JSON and recoverable from generated media metadata
Runs fully offline; --offline disables the paid API nodes
Loads checkpoints, separate diffusion models, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, ControlNets
weaknesses: Commits outside stable tags can break many custom nodes; stable releases roughly biweekly
GPL-3.0 license constrains embedding in proprietary products
NVIDIA 20-series and newer require PyTorch built with CUDA 13.0 or above
Paid partner and API nodes stay on unless --offline or --disable-partner-nodes is set

projects.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
projects.tagline: Turns a topic into a short video with script, footage, voiceover and subtitles
projects.summary: MoneyPrinterTurbo takes a topic or keywords and produces a finished short video. An LLM writes the script, footage comes from Pexels, Pixabay, Coverr, local files or text-to-video APIs, and TTS, subtitles and background music are added before the final render. It offers a WebUI, HTTP API, CLI and an agent skill, and outputs 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1.
strengths: Covers the whole pipeline: script, footage, voiceover, subtitles, music and render
Many LLM providers, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama for local models
Edge TTS needs no API key; Pexels and Pixabay stock footage are free
WebUI, API, CLI and batch generation; Docker and compose files included
weaknesses: Most LLMs and stock sources need API keys; AI video generation uses paid services
Footage relevance depends on keyword matching against stock libraries
README is dominated by sponsor and promotional sections
Web port and Docker setup details are not visible in the provided README

projects.name: InvokeAI
projects.tagline: Canvas-first web UI for Stable Diffusion and Flux image generation
projects.summary: Local web server and React UI for image generation with a Unified Canvas (inpainting, outpainting, brushes), a node-based workflow editor and a boards gallery with per-image metadata. Loads SD 1.5 to SD 3.5, SDXL, Flux.1 and Flux.2 variants, Qwen Image, Z-Image, Krea 2 and CogView 4 in ckpt, diffusers and some GGUF formats; Nano Banana, GPT Image and Wan are API-only. For artists iterating on images.
strengths: Unified Canvas with in/outpainting, brush tools and SAM/SAM2 segmentation
Broad model list including Flux.2 Dev and Klein, SD 3.5 Large, Qwen Image Edit
Apache-2.0 license; serves as the base for commercial products
Dedicated launcher application handles install and updates
weaknesses: No Dockerfile or compose file at the repo root; install goes through the Launcher
README lists features only; ports, hardware needs and env vars are in external docs
Video generation (Wan) is API-only, not local
Nano Banana and GPT Image require third-party API access

projects.name: AI Toolkit
projects.tagline: Fine-tuning suite for image, video and audio diffusion models, with GUI and CLI
projects.summary: AI Toolkit trains LoRA and LoKr adapters for diffusion models, covering FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Wan 2.1/2.2, LTX-2 and SDXL, plus audio models like ACE-Step 1.5. Jobs are defined in YAML and run with `python run.py`, or started and monitored from a web UI on port 8675. The UI can be protected with an AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH token, and training can also run on Modal or RunPod.
strengths: Supports a wide range of image, edit, video and audio models in one tool
Same YAML configs work from the CLI or the web UI
Training resumes from the last checkpoint after interruption
Layer targeting via only_if_contains and ignore_if_contains, plus LoKr support
weaknesses: Manual install requires an Nvidia GPU; Mac support is experimental
Install manager is labeled experimental by the author
Dataset images must be jpg, jpeg or png; webp has known issues
Ctrl+C during a checkpoint save can corrupt that checkpoint

projects.name: biniou
projects.tagline: Gradio web UI for local text, image, audio, video and 3D generation
projects.summary: biniou is a self-hosted Gradio web UI that bundles many generative modules: a llama-cpp chatbot for GGUF models, Whisper speech-to-text, Stable Diffusion and Flux image generation, MusicGen audio, video and Shap-E 3D. It runs on CPU from 8GB RAM, with optional CUDA or experimental ROCm, and can work offline once models are downloaded. Installers exist for several Linux distributions and Windows, plus a Dockerfile.
strengths: Covers text, image, audio, video and 3D generation in one UI
Runs on CPU only, from 8GB RAM; CUDA and experimental ROCm optional
One-click installers for several Linux distros and Windows; Dockerfile provided
Modules can pass outputs to each other; generation settings saved as metadata
weaknesses: AMD64 only; macOS support is experimental and untested
Many modules need 16GB+ RAM; about 200GB of disk with default models
Python 3.10 or 3.11 required; Windows install adds Visual Studio Build tools
Chatbot has no stated agents, tools or document chat; the README lists only chat and multimodal

projects.name: faceswap
projects.tagline: Python tool that trains neural models to swap faces in images and video
projects.summary: FaceSwap is a Python program with three stages run through `faceswap.py`: extract faces from photos or video frames, train a model on two sets of faces, and convert source media with the trained model. It ships a Tkinter-style GUI (`faceswap.py gui`) alongside the CLI, and includes models such as Villain and Phaze-A. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, with CUDA GPUs recommended and some AMD support via ROCm on Linux.
strengths: Covers the full workflow: extract, train and convert, via CLI or GUI
Multiple model architectures named in the README, including Villain, Phaze-A, DFL-H128 and DFaker
Runs on Windows, Linux and macOS; AMD GPUs supported via ROCm on Linux
Existing models can be reused to shorten training on new faces
weaknesses: Training requires a modern CUDA GPU for acceptable speed; exact VRAM needs are unknown
No Docker or compose setup in the repo
Setup problems are directed to the forum and Discord, not GitHub issues
Manual workflow: gathering and curating face data is left to the user

projects.name: Kohya's GUI
projects.tagline: Gradio GUI and CLI for Kohya diffusion training scripts
projects.summary: Wraps kohya-ss/sd-scripts in a Gradio UI that builds the training command for LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, DreamBooth, full fine-tuning, Textual Inversion and LECO concept erasure. Base models include SD 1.5/2.x, SDXL, SD3, Flux.1, Lumina Image 2.0, Anima and HunyuanImage-2.1. Installs with uv or pip, runs headless over SSH on a port such as 7860, ships Docker, Runpod and Colab paths, and suits people training their own LoRAs.
strengths: Covers LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, DreamBooth, fine-tune, Textual Inversion and LECO
GUI shell runs offline after install; no CDN assets or analytics by default
config.toml presets default paths and Gradio allowed_paths
Sample image generation during training with per-prompt seed, size and CFG flags
weaknesses: Needs a GPU-equipped machine; README gives no VRAM figures per model
Without --headless, OS file dialogs on the server can block training over SSH
macOS support is community-maintained and may vary
Last commit July 2026; sd-scripts submodule pinned to v0.11.1

projects.name: Pixelle-Video
projects.tagline: Topic-to-short-video pipeline built on ComfyUI workflows and TTS
projects.summary: Turns a topic into a short video: an LLM (GPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama) writes the script, ComfyUI or RunningHub workflows or direct APIs (DashScope Wan, GPT Image, Seedream, Seedance, Kling) produce per-sentence images or clips, Edge-TTS or Index-TTS voices it, and HTML templates lay out each frame. Streamlit UI on port 8501, plus digital-human and image-to-video modules. For creators already running ComfyUI.
strengths: Zero-cost path: Ollama for the LLM plus a local ComfyUI instance
Image, video, TTS and VLM steps are swappable ComfyUI workflows or direct APIs
Custom HTML templates for static, image-backed and video-backed layouts
Windows one-click package bundles Python, uv and ffmpeg
weaknesses: README and docs are Chinese first; an English README exists separately
Local image or video generation needs a running ComfyUI server (default port 8188)
Last commit June 2026; update log stops at 2026-06-01
Heavy local footprint: ComfyUI plus diffusion and TTS models

projects.name: FluxGym
projects.tagline: Web UI for training FLUX LoRAs on 12 to 20 GB GPUs
projects.summary: Gradio front end (forked from AI-Toolkit) over Kohya sd-scripts that trains FLUX.1-dev LoRAs with 12 GB, 16 GB or 20 GB VRAM presets. Upload images, caption them with a trigger word and press start; base models download automatically and an Advanced tab exposes every sd-scripts flag. Runs via Pinokio, a manual venv or docker compose on port 7860, for hobbyists training FLUX LoRAs on consumer GPUs.
strengths: VRAM presets for 12, 16 and 20 GB cards
Advanced tab is generated from sd-scripts flags, so every option is reachable
Sample images every N steps with fixed seeds to watch the LoRA evolve
Publish trained LoRAs to Hugging Face from the UI
weaknesses: FLUX.1 only (dev, dev2pro, schnell); schnell results are called not recommended
Manual install clones sd-scripts separately and uses PyTorch nightly builds
Docker image must be built locally; PUID and PGID must match your user
Last commit July 2026

projects.name: upscayl
projects.tagline: Desktop image upscaler using Real-ESRGAN models over Vulkan
projects.summary: Upscayl is an Electron desktop app that enlarges low-resolution images with Real-ESRGAN-based models run through an NCNN Vulkan backend. It supports batch upscaling, GPU selection by ID, and custom models converted from other formats. Installers cover Windows 10+, macOS 12+ and Linux (AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, deb, rpm).
strengths: Native installers for Windows, macOS and Linux, including Flatpak, Snap, AUR and Homebrew
Batch upscaling and selectable GPU ID in the GUI
Custom models can be added; a separate repo of extra models and a conversion guide exist
Separate upscayl-ncnn CLI backend is open source under AGPLv3
weaknesses: Requires a Vulkan-compatible GPU; many integrated GPUs do not work
Cannot de-blur or fix focus; it only enhances low-resolution or pixelated images
Last tagged release is 2024-12-25, though commits continue into 2026
Image upscaling only; no video or generation features described

projects.name: Strix
projects.tagline: Autonomous AI pentesting agents that validate findings with working exploits
projects.summary: CLI that runs a team of LLM agents (recon, exploitation, post-exploitation) against a local codebase, GitHub repo, live URL or OpenAPI/Postman spec. Agents work in a Docker sandbox with a Caido HTTP proxy, a Playwright browser, a shell and a Python exploit runtime, and each finding needs a working proof-of-concept. Installed by a curl script (PyPI package strix-agent); STRIX_LLM takes LiteLLM-style model strings, so OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter or a local Ollama/LM Studio endpoint all work.
strengths: Each finding is validated with a working proof-of-concept exploit, not just a pattern match
Targets code, GitHub repos, live URLs, OpenAPI/Swagger and Postman specs, or a target list
Headless mode exits non-zero on findings; GitHub Actions runs scope to changed files
Local web viewer (strix view) reads run results from disk, bound to 127.0.0.1
weaknesses: Needs Docker running; the first run pulls the sandbox image
Requires an LLM API key; local models only via LLM_API_BASE (Ollama, LM Studio)
Autofix PRs, continuous scanning and Jira/Slack hooks are Cloud; SSO and compliance reports are Enterprise
README documents install only as curl | bash, though a PyPI package (strix-agent) exists

projects.name: langchain
projects.tagline: Python framework for building LLM agents and apps from interoperable components
projects.summary: LangChain is a Python library that gives a standard interface to chat models, embeddings, vector stores and tools, so providers can be swapped with little code change. Models load through init_chat_model with a provider:model string. For lower-level agent orchestration it points to LangGraph, and for tracing and evals to LangSmith.
strengths: Common interface across model providers, embeddings and vector stores
Large integrations library covering tools, retrievers and vector stores
Companions: LangGraph for orchestration, Deep Agents for planning and subagents
MIT license; JS/TS counterpart available as LangChain.js
weaknesses: Observability, evals and managed deployment sit in LangSmith, a separate product
Controllable stateful agent workflows need LangGraph, not core LangChain
README gives no hardware requirements or list of supported providers
Abstraction layer is another API to learn on top of provider SDKs

projects.name: browser-use
projects.tagline: Python library that lets an LLM agent control a web browser
projects.summary: Browser Use runs an LLM-driven agent that opens a browser, reads pages and completes tasks such as searching, filling forms and booking slots. It is used as a Python library (3.11+), as a CLI skill for agents like Claude Code, or through a hosted cloud API. It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama and its own BU2 model, on local or cloud browsers.
strengths: Works with a local Chrome profile, a cloud browser, or a remote browser over CDP
Custom tools register with a decorator; system prompt can be extended or overridden
Supports OpenAI, Anthropic and Google wrappers, plus local models via Ollama
Ships a CLI skill so existing coding agents can drive a browser
weaknesses: README recommends BU2, which needs a paid Browser Use API key
CAPTCHA and stealth handling rely on the paid cloud browser, with no guarantee
Profile sync copies cookies only, not local storage, IndexedDB or extensions
Hardware needs for local models are not stated in the README

projects.name: crewai
projects.tagline: Python framework for multi-agent workflows with role-based Crews and event-driven Flows
projects.summary: CrewAI is a Python framework for building multi-agent workflows. Crews are teams of role-based agents with goals, tools and tasks, run sequentially or under a hierarchical manager. Flows are event-driven workflows with typed state, branching and routing that can embed Crews. A CLI scaffolds JSON-defined crew projects, with a classic YAML scaffold still available.
strengths: Two models: autonomous Crews and explicit Flows with state, branching and or_/and_ triggers
CLI scaffolds projects; agents and tasks declared in JSONC or classic YAML
Covers tools, memory, knowledge, checkpointing, async execution and MCP/A2A support
MIT license; recent commit and release within days of listing
weaknesses: Managed deployment, governance and enterprise support are in the commercial AMP Suite
README has a telemetry section; opt-out details are not in the excerpt
Requires Python >=3.10 and <3.14 and uv; Windows may need C++ build tools
Web search example needs a separate Serper.dev API key

projects.name: agno
projects.tagline: Python SDK and runtime for building and serving agents behind a REST API
projects.summary: Agno is a Python framework for defining agents, plus the AgentOS runtime that serves them through a REST API with 50+ endpoints, SSE and websockets. Sessions, memory, knowledge and traces are stored in your own database, and a web UI manages the running platform. It includes JWT-based RBAC, human approval steps, cron scheduling, and interfaces for Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, AG-UI and A2A.
strengths: Runtime ships a REST API with 50+ endpoints, SSE and websockets
JWT-based RBAC and multi-tenant isolation included
100+ prebuilt toolkits plus OpenTelemetry tracing and audit logs
Starter templates for Docker, AWS, GCP, Azure, Fly, Render, Modal and Helm
weaknesses: Sends a telemetry event per agent run unless AGNO_TELEMETRY=false is set
README gives no RAM, GPU or port requirements
Starter templates live in separate repos, not in this one
Management UI hosting and licensing terms are not described in the README

projects.name: llama_index
projects.tagline: Python framework for RAG and agent apps over your own data
projects.summary: LlamaIndex is a Python toolkit that loads data from files, APIs and SQL, builds indices such as a vector store index, and exposes query engines and retrievers for LLM apps. The llama-index-core package is extended by over 300 integration packages for LLMs, embeddings and vector stores. The maintainers say their main focus has moved to the commercial LlamaParse platform, while the framework stays available as open source.
strengths: Over 300 integration packages for LLM, embedding and vector store providers
Small core package plus a starter bundle; install only the integrations needed
High-level API indexes and queries a directory in a few lines
Works with local models, e.g. Ollama LLMs and Hugging Face embeddings
weaknesses: README says company focus has shifted to the paid LlamaParse platform
README is noted as less up to date than the documentation
Index storage is in-memory by default; persistence to ./storage is manual
Library only: no UI, server or Docker setup included

projects.name: langgraph
projects.tagline: Python framework for building long-running, stateful agents as graphs
projects.summary: LangGraph is a low-level Python library for orchestrating stateful agents and workflows as graphs, inspired by Pregel and Apache Beam. It provides durable execution that resumes after failures, human-in-the-loop interrupts to inspect and edit state, and short-term and long-term memory. It can be used without LangChain; tracing and managed deployment go through the separate LangSmith products.
strengths: Durable execution resumes agents from where they stopped after a failure
Interrupts allow inspecting and modifying agent state mid-run
Built-in short-term and long-term memory across sessions
Usable without LangChain; a JS/TS port (LangGraph.js) also exists
weaknesses: Low-level API; higher-level agent building is pushed to the separate Deep Agents package
Tracing UI and managed deployment rely on LangSmith, a commercial LangChain product
No visual builder in this repo; agents are defined in code only
README gives no RAM, storage or persistence backend requirements

projects.name: openmanus
projects.tagline: Python agent that carries out terminal-entered tasks with LLM tools and a browser
projects.summary: OpenManus is a Python agent framework, an open reimplementation of Manus, that takes a task typed in the terminal and carries it out with tools. It drives a browser through the Browser Use CLI MCP server and calls an LLM endpoint configured in config.toml. Extra entry points cover an MCP tool version, an experimental multi-agent flow, and an optional data analysis agent.
strengths: Browser automation via Browser Use MCP server; local Chrome mode needs no API key
Separate entry points: main.py, run_mcp.py and run_flow.py for multi-agent
Simple config.toml with separate LLM and vision model settings
MIT license, active commits, and a Hugging Face demo space
weaknesses: Multi-agent flow is described by the README as unstable
Terminal-only interface, no web UI or user accounts
No tagged release since 2025-04-10
README shows only OpenAI-style API setup, no local model guidance

projects.name: metagpt
projects.tagline: Python multi-agent framework that turns one-line requirements into a software repo
projects.summary: MetaGPT assigns LLM-backed roles (product manager, architect, project manager, engineer) to follow predefined SOPs, turning a one-line requirement into user stories, designs, APIs and code. It runs as a CLI (`metagpt "Create a 2048 game"`) or a Python library, and also ships a Data Interpreter role for data analysis. LLM providers such as OpenAI, Azure, Ollama and Groq are set in `~/.metagpt/config2.yaml`.
strengths: Role and SOP model produces requirements, design docs and code repo from one prompt
Usable as CLI or Python library; pip install metagpt
Provider set in one YAML file: OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, Groq and others
MIT license with tutorials, agent and multi-agent guides, and research papers
weaknesses: Python 3.9 to below 3.12 only
Requires Node and pnpm installed before actual use
Last release was 2024-04-22; the PyPI package may lag the main branch
README calls the software-company schematic 'gradually implementing'

projects.name: autogen
projects.tagline: Python and .NET framework for multi-agent apps, now in maintenance mode
projects.summary: AutoGen is a layered framework for building multi-agent applications: a Core API for event-driven message passing, an AgentChat API for two-agent and group-chat patterns, and an Extensions API for model clients, MCP tools and code execution. It also ships AutoGen Studio, a no-code prototyping UI on port 8080, and AgentBench. The project is in maintenance mode and community managed; Microsoft points new users to Microsoft Agent Framework.
strengths: Layered design: Core, AgentChat and Extensions APIs let you pick the abstraction level
Core runtime supports local and distributed execution, with Python and .NET packages
MCP tool support through McpWorkbench, e.g. the Playwright MCP server
Includes AutoGen Studio for no-code prototyping and a benchmarking suite
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: no new features, only bug fixes, security patches and docs
Maintainers recommend Microsoft Agent Framework for new projects
AutoGen Studio is explicitly not production-ready and has no built-in authentication
Support is community-only and response times may be slow

projects.name: hindsight
projects.tagline: Agent memory server with retain, recall and reflect operations
projects.summary: Hindsight stores agent memories in banks and extracts facts, entities and timestamps from retained text using an LLM. Recall runs semantic, BM25, graph and temporal retrieval in parallel, then reranks the merged results. Background jobs consolidate facts into observations and mental models. It exposes a REST API, Python, Node.js and Go clients, a CLI, and a per-bank MCP endpoint.
strengths: Four parallel retrieval strategies merged with reciprocal rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking
Works with 25+ LLM providers, including local ollama, lmstudio and llamacpp
Built-in MCP endpoint per bank, plus 60+ listed integrations
Embedded mode runs in-process via pip with a bundled pg0 database
weaknesses: Every retain call requires an LLM, adding cost and latency
Accuracy claims are the vendor's own benchmarks; independent reproduction is partial
Managed Cloud and Enterprise tiers exist; feature differences from self-hosted are unclear
Minimum RAM and GPU needs are not stated in the README

projects.name: MemPalace
projects.tagline: Local long-term memory store for agents with verbatim storage and semantic search
projects.summary: MemPalace stores conversation history as verbatim text and retrieves it with semantic search, organized into wings (people, projects), rooms (topics) and drawers (original content). It ships a CLI, 47 MCP tools, a SQLite temporal knowledge graph, and auto-save hooks for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor. ChromaDB is the default backend; sqlite_exact, rust_exact, Milvus, Qdrant and pgvector are selectable.
strengths: Raw retrieval scores 96.6% R@5 on LongMemEval with no LLM or API key
Pluggable backends: Chroma, SQLite exact, Rust, Milvus, Qdrant, pgvector
Benchmark results and reproduction commands are committed in the repository
Optional OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint, including local LM Studio, llama.cpp or Ollama
weaknesses: Native Termux install unsupported; Android needs a Debian PRoot container
Stores verbatim text only; no summarization or fact extraction
First embedding call downloads a model of about 80 to 300 MB
GPU Docker image is not published and is x86_64-only

projects.name: Cognee
projects.tagline: Memory engine that turns documents and code into a knowledge graph
projects.summary: Cognee builds persistent agent memory by extracting entities, relationships and chunks from text, code and sessions into a graph and vector index with hybrid recall. Without an LLM key it uses local GLiNER extraction and embeddings; adding a key enables generated answers via OpenAI, Ollama or other providers. It runs as a library, CLI, REST API (port 8000), UI (3000) and MCP server (8001).
strengths: Keyless mode: local GLiNER extraction and embeddings, no cloud LLM required
Claude Code and Codex plugins, OpenClaw plugin, MCP server, Python, TypeScript and Rust SDKs
Imports memory from Mem0, Letta, Zep or Graphiti via the COGX format
Apache-2.0; research paper and BEAM evaluation published
weaknesses: Single-Postgres graph store is a demo; production version is a licensed product
API defaults to multi-tenant mode; local use needs ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL=false
Bundled GLiNER extractor is a demo; higher-accuracy version requires contacting the vendor
UI launcher needs Node.js/npm and Docker for its MCP service

projects.name: agentmemory
projects.tagline: Persistent memory server for coding agents, exposed over MCP and REST
projects.summary: agentmemory captures what a coding agent does across sessions, stores it as searchable memory, and injects relevant context at the start of the next session. It runs as a local Node.js server on the pinned iii engine and connects to agents through hooks, MCP, or REST, with 20 adapters listed. Keyless mode uses BM25 search; vector embeddings need a provider or the local Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model.
strengths: No external database; state lives in a local iii engine data directory
Works with 20 listed agents through hooks, MCP, or REST
Keyless BM25 mode works without any API key
Local embeddings via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local after a one-time model download
weaknesses: Keyless mode has no vector search, so semantic queries can return nothing
Pinned to iii-engine v0.22.1; refuses to attach to other engine versions
Native Windows needs manual iii.exe install; WSL2 or Docker recommended
Uses four local ports (3111, 3112, 3113, 49134)

projects.name: OpenViking
projects.tagline: Context database that stores agent memory, resources and skills as a virtual filesystem
projects.summary: OpenViking organizes what an agent knows under a viking:// virtual filesystem, with documents, memories and skills browsable through ls, tree, read, write and grep. Directories carry generated L0 abstracts and L1 overviews so agents read summaries before full content, and committed sessions become editable Markdown memories. It ships a server, an ov CLI, Python, Go and TypeScript SDKs, an HTTP API, and a memory plugin installer for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.
strengths: Memory is stored as inspectable, editable files under viking:// URIs rather than opaque embeddings
Search can be scoped to a directory subtree; L0/L1 summaries cut full reads
Plugin installer covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, TRAE, OpenCode, with OpenClaw and Hermes integrations
Python, Go and TypeScript SDKs, HTTP API, CLI, plus accounts, user isolation and opt-in ACLs
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license may constrain embedding in proprietary or networked products
Needs a model provider with both an embedding model and a VLM
Memory extraction runs in the background, so new memories are not immediately retrievable
Published benchmarks use Volcengine Doubao models; results with other providers are not shown

projects.name: Mem0
projects.tagline: Memory layer for agents with a self-hosted server, SDKs and CLI
projects.summary: Mem0 adds long-term memory to assistants and agents at user, session and agent level. It ships as a Python and npm library, a self-hosted server via docker compose (dashboard on port 3000, auth on by default) and a managed cloud. Memories are extracted by an LLM (gpt-5-mini by default) and retrieved with semantic, BM25 and entity matching; an optional NLP extra adds spaCy for hybrid search.
strengths: Library, self-hosted server with dashboard and API keys, or managed platform share one API
Multi-signal retrieval: semantic, BM25 keyword and entity matching with temporal reasoning
CLI and agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others
Apache-2.0; evaluation framework is open source
weaknesses: Requires an LLM for extraction; OpenAI gpt-5-mini and text-embedding-3-small are the defaults
Benchmark scores reflect the managed platform, not the open-source SDK
Self-hosted server exposes only teasers of advanced features; all included in cloud
Hybrid search recommends at least a 600M-parameter embedding model

projects.name: Graphiti
projects.tagline: Temporal knowledge graph framework for agent memory with REST and MCP servers
projects.summary: Graphiti builds context graphs where every fact has a validity window and traces back to its source episode, ingesting text and JSON incrementally. Retrieval fuses embeddings, BM25 and graph traversal. It needs a graph database (Neo4j, FalkorDB or Neptune) and defaults to OpenAI, with Anthropic, Gemini, Groq and OpenAI-compatible servers supported; REST and MCP servers ship in the repo.
strengths: Bi-temporal facts: old facts are invalidated, not deleted, so history stays queryable
Hybrid retrieval combines embeddings, BM25 and graph traversal with sub-second latency claims
Custom entity and edge types via Pydantic models
Docker Compose profiles for Neo4j or FalkorDB; MCP and REST servers included
weaknesses: Requires Neo4j, FalkorDB or Amazon Neptune plus OpenSearch; Kuzu is deprecated
Defaults to OpenAI; needs structured-output models, smaller models may fail ingestion
Default SEMAPHORE_LIMIT of 10 keeps ingestion slow to avoid 429 errors
Users, threads and dashboards are left to the commercial Zep platform

projects.name: Supermemory
projects.tagline: Memory and context API that extracts user facts and serves profiles to agents
projects.summary: Supermemory extracts facts from conversations, tracks updates and contradictions, expires stale facts, and returns a per-user profile plus hybrid RAG and memory search through one API. It ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, an MCP server, plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode, and connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive and GitHub. A local server (default port 6767) runs against any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Ollama model.
strengths: Single call returns user profile (static and dynamic facts) plus search results, claimed ~50ms
Local server exposes the same API as the hosted platform; switch by changing baseURL
Handles contradictions and expiry of temporary facts instead of only appending
Wrappers for Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, Mastra, OpenAI Agents SDK, n8n
weaknesses: Benchmark claims (#1 on LongMemEval, LoCoMo, ConvoMem) are self-reported
URL ingestion in local mode relies on a hosted reader service
MCP server and plugins default to the hosted service at mcp.supermemory.ai
Local edition differs from Enterprise; README defers details to a separate docs page

projects.name: MemOS
projects.tagline: Memory operating system for agents with cubes, scheduler and hybrid retrieval
projects.summary: MemOS gives LLM apps and agents long-term memory via one API over graph-structured memories, grouped into memory cubes per user, project or agent. Self-hosting runs docker compose for the REST API on port 8000 with Neo4j and Qdrant; a local plugin for OpenClaw, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness instead keeps everything in SQLite with FTS5 and vector search.
strengths: Memory cubes isolate or share knowledge across users, projects and agents
MemScheduler ingests asynchronously for high-concurrency workloads
Local plugin for OpenClaw, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness is 100% on-device SQLite
Apache-2.0; two arXiv papers and OmniMemEval benchmark published
weaknesses: Self-hosted service requires Neo4j and Qdrant
Local plugin docs are partly in Chinese; cloud dashboard links go to a cn locale
LLM, embedder and vector DB keys must be filled in .env before start
Benchmark table lists scores without comparison baselines in the README

projects.name: Engram
projects.tagline: Persistent memory store for AI coding agents, exposed over MCP
projects.summary: Engram is a single Go binary that stores coding-agent memory in a local SQLite database with FTS5 search. It exposes save, search, timeline and session tools over MCP stdio, plus a CLI, local HTTP API and terminal UI. `engram setup <agent>` configures 14 targets including Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf. Git Sync and an optional Engram Cloud handle sharing across machines.
strengths: Single Go binary with one SQLite file; no Node, Python or Docker required
One setup command per agent, 14 targets plus any MCP-compatible client
Project-aware: resolves project from explicit flag, ENGRAM_PROJECT or cwd
Local database is authoritative; Git Sync exports compressed chunks for sharing
weaknesses: Aimed at coding agents; not a general-purpose memory layer for other assistants
Search is SQLite FTS5 full-text; README mentions no embedding or vector search
Cloud replication is a separate optional component with its own upgrade steps
Codex integration needs a compatible running core and manual restart after upgrades

projects.name: Honcho
projects.tagline: Memory server that builds per-peer representations from agent conversations
projects.summary: Honcho is a FastAPI memory service that stores messages on sessions, reasons over them in a background queue, and returns peer representations, session context, hybrid BM25 plus vector search, or natural-language answers. It ships Python and TypeScript SDKs, a CLI, and plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo Code and OpenClaw. It runs as a managed service at api.honcho.dev or self-hosted with API, deriver, Postgres and Redis.
strengths: Peer model covers users, agents, groups and projects, including what one peer knows about another
Python and TypeScript SDKs; context exports directly to OpenAI or Anthropic message formats
First-party plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo Code and OpenClaw share one config file
Hybrid BM25 plus vector search and a low-latency representation endpoint alongside the chat endpoint
weaknesses: Reasoning runs asynchronously, so new messages may not appear in chat results immediately
Self-hosting needs an LLM provider key (Gemini, Anthropic or OpenAI) for the background deriver
AGPL-3.0 license may restrict use in closed-source network services
Self-hosted stack requires Postgres and Redis alongside the API and deriver processes

projects.name: Letta
projects.tagline: Stateful agent harness with git-tracked memory, channels and remote computers
projects.summary: Letta Code is an npm-installed agent harness whose agents keep memory blocks, skills and prompts in a git-tracked MemFS and rewrite them over time. Agents run from a CLI, desktop app, browser (chat.letta.com) or Telegram, Slack and Discord channels, use subagents, hooks and cron schedules, and can run on remote machines via letta server. Letta Cloud is the default backend; local is available.
strengths: All agent context including memory blocks is versioned in git (MemFS)
Same agent reachable from CLI, desktop, browser, Telegram, Slack and Discord
Skills installable from GitHub, ClawHub or the Hermes Skills Hub
Apache-2.0; Nix flake and AUR packages available
weaknesses: Letta Cloud is the default; remote computers and secrets require signing in
Self-hosted app server setup is not described in the README; local backend only mentioned
AgentFile export/import removed; agent registry imports no longer supported
Automatic dreaming is disabled on native Windows by default

projects.name: LocalAI
projects.tagline: One OpenAI-compatible server for text, speech, image and video models
projects.summary: LocalAI is a Go server on port 8080 with OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs and Ollama-compatible APIs for text, vision, speech, image and video. Backends (llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, whisper.cpp, diffusers, MLX, 60+ total) ship as separate OCI images pulled on demand; containers exist for CPU, CUDA, ROCm, Intel and Vulkan. It adds API keys, quotas and OIDC, agents with MCP, and a PostgreSQL/NATS distributed mode.
strengths: Small core; 60+ backends installed on demand as OCI images
OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs and Ollama API compatibility in one server
Multi-user: API keys, per-user quotas, role-based access, OIDC
Container images for CPU, CUDA 12/13, ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Vulkan, Jetson
weaknesses: First model load pulls backend images; needs network and disk space
macOS DMG is unsigned and needs quarantine removal
Distributed mode requires PostgreSQL and NATS
Very wide scope (agents, biometrics, video) increases configuration surface

projects.name: llama.cpp
projects.tagline: C/C++ inference engine serving GGUF models over an OpenAI-compatible API
projects.summary: llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine for LLMs and VLMs with no dependencies, built on ggml. llama serve starts an OpenAI-compatible API server with a built-in web UI, pulling GGUF models straight from Hugging Face, with 1.5 to 8-bit quantization and CPU+GPU hybrid offload for models larger than VRAM. Backends cover CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, CANN, MUSA and WebGPU.
strengths: Plain C/C++ with no runtime dependencies; prebuilt binaries and Docker
Backends for NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Metal, Intel SYCL, Vulkan, Ascend, Moore Threads
Hybrid CPU+GPU offload runs models larger than available VRAM
Built-in web UI and OpenAI-compatible server via llama serve
weaknesses: GGUF model format only
README gives no port, auth or sizing guidance; see tools/server docs
Install script is curl piped to sh; otherwise build from source
OpenVINO backend still in progress

projects.name: Ollama
projects.tagline: Runs open-weight models locally behind a CLI and REST API
projects.summary: Ollama runs open-weight models locally with a CLI and a REST API on port 11434, pulling models from its own library (for example gemma4) and using llama.cpp as the inference backend. Install scripts cover macOS, Windows and Linux, and an official Docker image exists. The ollama launch command wires it into coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and OpenCode, or into OpenClaw as a chat assistant.
strengths: One command pulls and runs a model; REST API on 11434
Official Docker image plus Python and JavaScript libraries
ollama launch integrates with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode
Broad ecosystem: dozens of web, desktop and IDE clients listed
weaknesses: Single inference backend: llama.cpp
Install is a curl piped to sh script
README gives no RAM or VRAM guidance per model size
Models come from Ollama's own registry; others need import steps

projects.name: vLLM
projects.tagline: Inference engine for Hugging Face LLMs with PagedAttention and continuous batching
projects.summary: vLLM is a Python library and server for LLM inference. It manages attention KV memory with PagedAttention, batches requests continuously, and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API, plus the Anthropic Messages API and gRPC. It supports 200+ Hugging Face model architectures and runs on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs, several CPU types, and other accelerators through plugins.
strengths: Continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching and PagedAttention for high-throughput serving
Wide quantization support: FP8, NVFP4, INT4/INT8, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF and others
Tensor, pipeline, data, expert and context parallelism for multi-GPU inference
Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs, with plugins for TPU, Gaudi, Ascend
weaknesses: README gives no minimum RAM or VRAM figures
Several hardware targets depend on separate plugins rather than the core package
Large feature surface means many tuning options to learn
Server and library only, with no built-in chat UI

projects.name: colibri
projects.tagline: C inference engine that runs huge MoE models by streaming experts from disk
projects.summary: colibri runs large mixture-of-experts models such as GLM-5.2 (744B) and Kimi K3 (2.8T) on ordinary hardware. It keeps the dense weights in RAM and reads routed experts from disk through a cache, with optional Vulkan or CUDA offload. It serves a browser dashboard plus OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible HTTP endpoints, and ships guided setup scripts for Windows, Linux and macOS.
strengths: Pure C engines, no GPU required; 8 GB RAM minimum for the smallest model
Serves OpenAI and Anthropic-style APIs on port 8000, plus a web dashboard
Vulkan works on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA; CUDA path for NVIDIA on Linux and Windows
Setup script detects hardware, recommends a model, and resumes interrupted downloads
weaknesses: Large models stream from disk: 0.05-3 tok/s on typical machines, per README tables
Discrete-GPU performance mostly unmeasured by the authors; relies on user reports
Supports a fixed list of model families, one engine each; other architectures need new code
Some models need manual conversion or preparation steps after download

projects.name: SGLang
projects.tagline: Inference server for LLM, vision-language and diffusion models
projects.summary: SGLang is a Python inference framework for serving large language, vision-language and diffusion models, aimed at agentic workloads, large-scale serving and RL rollouts. It runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Intel, Apple Silicon, Huawei Ascend and Moore Threads hardware, and includes a built-in engine for image and video generation. Install via the lmsysorg/sglang Docker image or uv pip.
strengths: Supports NVIDIA, AMD, TPU, Intel, Apple Silicon, Ascend and Moore Threads hardware
Image and video diffusion engine ships in the same package
Integrated by RL training frameworks such as verl and slime for rollouts
Apache-2.0 license, with a Docker image and a cookbook of launch commands
weaknesses: Audio TTS/ASR serving lives in a separate project, SGLang Omni
Install requires --prerelease=allow with uv, suggesting prerelease dependencies
Several hardware backends (Trainium, Cambricon, MetaX) are still in progress
README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements; sizing depends on model and hardware

projects.name: Lemonade
projects.tagline: Local AI server that targets GPUs and AMD NPUs with OpenAI-style APIs
projects.summary: Lemonade is a local AI server with OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama-compatible APIs on port 13305 that runs GGUF, FLM and ONNX models, Whisper transcription, Kokoro speech and Stable Diffusion images. It picks the backend for the hardware: llama.cpp on CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm or Metal, plus AMD XDNA2 NPU paths for Ryzen AI. Packages exist for Windows, macOS, Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu, Arch, Snap and Docker.
strengths: NPU backends for AMD XDNA2 (Ryzen AI) alongside CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal
Chat, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image and audio generation in one server
Native packages: msi, pkg, deb, rpm, Arch, Snap, PPA, Docker
Model aliases enable active-standby failover between models
weaknesses: Many engines (vllm, ds4, openmoss, trellis) are marked experimental
NPU support covers AMD XDNA2 only
macOS gets Metal only; several backends are Windows or Linux only
Cloud offload to OpenAI-compatible providers is experimental

projects.name: exo
projects.tagline: Distributed LLM inference across Macs and other devices, MLX-based
projects.summary: exo joins devices on a network into one inference cluster, splitting a model across them with pipeline or tensor parallelism based on a live view of topology. It uses MLX for inference and exposes OpenAI Chat Completions, Claude Messages, OpenAI Responses and Ollama-compatible APIs plus a built-in dashboard on port 52415. On Macs with Thunderbolt 5 and macOS 26.2 or later, it can use RDMA between nodes.
strengths: Runs models too large for one machine by sharding across devices
Devices discover each other automatically, no manual cluster config
Serves OpenAI, Claude Messages, Responses and Ollama-style APIs
Tensor parallelism reported up to 1.8x on 2 devices, 3.2x on 4
weaknesses: On Linux, inference currently runs on CPU only; GPU support is in development
RDMA needs macOS 26.2+, Thunderbolt 5, a Recovery-mode setting and identical OS versions
Source install needs Rust nightly, Node and uv; no Docker image detected
Models are MLX-format; GGUF support is not mentioned in the README

projects.name: Xinference
projects.tagline: Serves LLM, embedding, speech and image models behind one OpenAI-compatible API
projects.summary: Xinference is a Python library and server that runs language, embedding, speech recognition, image and multimodal models from a single command, with built-in model definitions and support for custom ones. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API with function calling, plus RPC, a CLI and a web UI, and can spread models across multiple workers. It runs on GPUs and CPUs through backends including vLLM and its own llama.cpp binding.
strengths: One server covers LLM, embedding, audio, image and multimodal models
OpenAI-compatible REST API with function calling
Distributed inference across workers; Helm chart for Kubernetes
Install via pip, one-line script, Docker or Helm
weaknesses: Enterprise, Cloud and managed Model API offerings are commercial; edition differences not listed
3.0.0 release notes mention breaking changes and migration steps
RAM and VRAM requirements are not stated; they depend on the model
README feature list is dense; hardware and backend support per model is unclear

projects.name: llama-swap
projects.tagline: Go proxy that starts and swaps local inference servers per request
projects.summary: llama-swap is a single Go binary that sits in front of local inference servers such as llama.cpp, vllm, stable-diffusion.cpp and audio.cpp. It reads the `model` field of each OpenAI- or Anthropic-style request, starts the matching server from a YAML `cmd`, and stops the previous one. It includes a web UI, API keys, TTL unloading and a matrix DSL for running models concurrently.
strengths: One binary and one YAML file, no external dependencies
Works with any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible upstream server, not only llama.cpp
Matrix DSL runs chosen models concurrently; ttl unloads idle ones
Built-in web UI with playground, token metrics, log streaming and Prometheus /metrics
weaknesses: Does not run inference itself; you supply and configure the upstream servers
Originally designed for llama-server; Python servers like vllm should run in Docker or Podman
Swapping reloads the model, so the first request after a switch is slow
Auth is limited to API keys; no user accounts mentioned

projects.name: Triton Inference Server
projects.tagline: NVIDIA inference server for TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX and more over HTTP/gRPC
projects.summary: Triton serves TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX, OpenVINO, Python and RAPIDS FIL models over HTTP/REST and gRPC (KServe v2), with concurrent execution, dynamic and sequence batching, ensembles and Business Logic Scripting. NVIDIA ships it as NGC containers (2.73.0 / 26.09) for NVIDIA GPUs, x86 and ARM CPUs, Jetson and AWS Inferentia, with C and Java in-process APIs and a metrics endpoint.
strengths: Serves TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX, OpenVINO, Python and FIL models together
Dynamic and sequence batching, ensembles and BLS pipelines
HTTP/REST and gRPC (KServe v2) plus C and Java in-process APIs
Metrics for GPU utilization, throughput and latency
weaknesses: No OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the README; clients speak KServe v2
Model repository and per-model config files are hand-written
Containers track NVIDIA's monthly NGC release cycle
Not every backend is supported on every platform

projects.name: mistral.rs
projects.tagline: Rust inference server with OpenAI and Anthropic APIs and agent tools
projects.summary: mistral.rs is a Rust engine whose single binary runs and serves Hugging Face, GGUF and UQFF models (text, vision, video, audio, speech, image generation; 45+ architectures) with auto-detected architecture and chat template. The serve command exposes OpenAI /v1 and Anthropic Messages endpoints, a web UI at /ui and Prometheus metrics on port 1234, with paged attention, ISQ, LoRA and a built-in agent loop.
strengths: One binary for chat, server, benchmarks and web UI; prebuilt for Metal, CUDA, CPU
In-situ quantization of any Hugging Face model plus GGUF 2-8 bit, GPTQ, AWQ, FP8
Server-side agent loop with Python, shell, web search, skills and MCP client
mistralrs tune recommends quantization and device mapping for your hardware
weaknesses: BF16 prefill trails vLLM by 5-10x on the 26B MoE in its own benchmarks
Install script is curl piped to sh, falling back to a source build
cuTile acceleration needs NVIDIA's separately installed tileiras tool
Not affiliated with Mistral AI despite the name

projects.name: GPUStack
projects.tagline: GPU cluster manager that deploys models on vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM
projects.summary: GPUStack is a GPU cluster manager that deploys models across on-prem, Kubernetes and cloud workers, configuring vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or custom engines behind OpenAI-compatible APIs with auth, API keys and token metering. The server is one Docker container on port 80 and can run CPU-only; Linux workers join with a privileged Docker command. It supports NVIDIA, AMD, Ascend and six Chinese accelerator families.
strengths: Multi-cluster: on-prem, Kubernetes and cloud GPUs under one server
Auto-selects and tunes vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM per model
Built-in auth, API keys, token metering, Grafana and Prometheus dashboards
SSH-accessible GPU instances on demand for fine-tuning
weaknesses: Workers are Linux-only; macOS cannot be a worker, Windows needs WSL2
Worker container runs privileged with the Docker socket mounted
Cluster topology view is in the paid GPUStack Enterprise
Quick start assumes an NVIDIA GPU; other vendors need extra steps

projects.name: laya-mlx
projects.tagline: MLX port of Laya typed-decision models for Apple Silicon
projects.summary: Runs the Laya encoder checkpoints (322M to 421M parameters) natively on Apple Silicon with MLX. It answers typed questions (choice, score, true/false probability) in one forward pass with zero output tokens. Reported M3 Max median latency is 13.4 ms for the English model and 7.4 ms for the multilingual one. It is an independent port covering inference and conversion, not training.
strengths: Single forward pass, no token decoding or JSON generation; P50 13.42 ms English on M3 Max
Matched upstream answers on 63/63 validation questions in FP32 and FP16 per checkpoint
No PyTorch, Transformers runtime or cloud API; runs locally after first weight download
Includes language router, confidence gating, shortlist and tournament helpers for large choice sets
weaknesses: Apple Silicon only (macOS 14+, Python 3.11+); no CUDA or Linux path
Limited to choice, score and noul questions; not a general text-generation server
No training or fine-tuning; upstream batch, HTTP/MCP server and hooks APIs are not included
Context capped at 512 or 1,024 tokens; many-label choices need shortlisting or tournament

projects.name: KTransformers
projects.tagline: CPU-GPU hybrid inference and LoRA fine-tuning for large MoE models
projects.summary: KTransformers runs large Mixture-of-Experts models by keeping hot experts on the GPU and cold experts on the CPU, using AMX/AVX512/AVX2 INT4/INT8 kernels with NUMA-aware memory. The kt-kernel package plugs into SGLang for serving. A second path integrates with LLaMA-Factory for LoRA and full fine-tuning of MoE models such as DeepSeek-V3/R1 and Kimi K2.5 on limited GPU memory.
strengths: Runs very large MoE models with experts offloaded to CPU RAM, so fewer GPUs are needed
CPU kernels cover Intel AMX, AVX512 and AVX2-only machines
Fine-tuning via LLaMA-Factory; README lists DeepSeek-V3 at ~80GB total GPU memory on 4x RTX 4090
Fast support for new models, with tutorials for GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, MiniMax and DeepSeek-V4-Flash
weaknesses: Needs large system RAM for big MoE models; exact minimum is not stated in the README
Original integrated framework is archived; the current docs are split across kt-kernel and SFT
Serving depends on SGLang integration rather than a standalone server in this README
Research-oriented project; setup is manual, with per-model tutorials and hardware-specific steps

projects.name: LMDeploy
projects.tagline: LLM and VLM serving toolkit with the TurboMind and PyTorch engines
projects.summary: LMDeploy compresses and serves LLMs and VLMs with two engines: TurboMind (CUDA, persistent batching, blocked KV cache, AWQ W4A16, MXFP4) and a pure-Python PyTorch engine that also runs on Huawei Ascend. pip install lmdeploy adds an API server plus a proxy for multi-model, multi-machine serving. Models span Llama, Qwen3, DeepSeek-V3/V4, GLM-5, InternVL and Qwen3-VL.
strengths: TurboMind engine with persistent batching, blocked KV cache and 4-bit AWQ inference
Online INT8/INT4 KV cache quantization and prefix caching usable together
Wide VLM list: InternVL 1 to 3.5, Qwen2/2.5/3-VL, LLaVA, Gemma3, Llama4
PyTorch engine supports Huawei Ascend NPUs with graph mode
weaknesses: The two engines support different model sets and dtypes; check the matrix
Prebuilt wheels target CUDA 12.8; other CUDA versions need source builds
No port, VRAM or web UI details in the README
Community channels are WeChat-centric alongside Discord

projects.name: Text Generation Web UI
projects.tagline: Local LLM chat UI and API with five switchable loader backends
projects.summary: TextGen runs local LLMs behind a chat UI and an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API with tool calling and MCP, with llama.cpp, ik_llama.cpp, Transformers, ExLlamaV3 or TensorRT-LLM loaders switchable without restart. Portable builds for Linux, Windows and macOS bundle CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm or CPU dependencies for GGUF; the full install adds LoRA training, image generation and extensions. Web UI on port 7860.
strengths: Portable builds with all dependencies for CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm and CPU
Five loaders switchable without restarting
OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible API with tool calling and MCP servers
LoRA training and diffusers image generation in the same app
weaknesses: Full install needs ~10 GB disk and PyTorch; portable build is GGUF only
Multi-user mode does not save chat histories; meant for small trusted teams
Docker needs per-GPU Dockerfile symlinks and manual .env edits
AGPL-3.0 license

projects.name: llamafile
projects.tagline: Single-file executables that bundle llama.cpp with model weights
projects.summary: llamafile packages llama.cpp and model weights into one executable using Cosmopolitan Libc, so a downloaded .llamafile runs on Linux, macOS, Windows and BSD across CPU architectures with no install and serves a local web UI and API. Since 0.10 it tracks upstream llama.cpp closely for newer models, and whisperfile applies the same packaging to speech-to-text. Maintained by Mozilla.ai.
strengths: Single file, no installation, runs across OSes and CPU architectures
0.10 build system tracks upstream llama.cpp for recent model support
Can run external GGUF weights with the bare llamafile binary
whisperfile gives single-file transcription and translation
weaknesses: Windows cannot run executables above 4 GB; larger models need external weights
0.10.x dropped some classic features; older releases remain for those
Pre-built llamafiles limited to Mozilla.ai's Hugging Face uploads
One model per file; not a multi-model server

projects.name: Text Embeddings Inference
projects.tagline: Rust server for embedding, reranker and classification models
projects.summary: TEI is a Rust server from Hugging Face for embedding, reranker and sequence-classification models (BERT, XLM-RoBERTa, Nomic, Jina, GTE, Qwen3, ModernBERT, Gemma3) with token-based dynamic batching and Flash Attention. The router listens on port 3000 with /embed and OpenAI-compatible routes, gRPC, OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus metrics. Images cover CPU x86/arm64 and NVIDIA Turing through Blackwell.
strengths: Token-based dynamic batching with Flash Attention, Candle and cuBLASLt
Small images and fast boot; no graph compilation step
Rerankers and classifiers served alongside embeddings
OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics, API key auth, gRPC
weaknesses: No Volta support; Turing image is experimental with Flash Attention off
GPU images need drivers compatible with CUDA 12.2 or higher
Only CamemBERT and XLM-RoBERTa for sequence classification
7B embedders such as Qwen3-Embedding-8B are flagged very expensive

projects.name: TabbyAPI
projects.tagline: OpenAI-compatible API server for running ExLlamaV3 models
projects.summary: TabbyAPI is a FastAPI server that loads and serves LLMs through the ExLlamaV3 backend, exposing an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API. It supports runtime model loading and unloading, HuggingFace downloads, embedding models, constrained output (JSON schema, regex, EBNF), and tool calling. The README describes it as a hobby project for a small user base, not for production servers.
strengths: Continuous batching with paged attention on Nvidia Ampere and newer GPUs
Speculative decoding with draft models; JSON schema, regex and EBNF constraints
Load, unload and download models at runtime without restarting the server
Published Docker images for CUDA 12.8, CUDA 13 and ROCm
weaknesses: README says it is not meant for production servers
Only EXL3 and FP16/BF16 models; no GGUF support listed
Rolling release with no tagged releases; dependencies may need reinstalling
AGPL-3.0 license may restrict use in some network services

projects.name: bitnet
projects.tagline: Inference framework for 1.58-bit ternary LLMs on CPU and GPU
projects.summary: bitnet.cpp is Microsoft's llama.cpp-based inference framework with optimized I2_S, TL1 and TL2 kernels for ternary BitNet b1.58 models on x86 and ARM CPUs, plus a GPU kernel. It runs GGUF models through Python scripts for setup, chat and benchmarking. The README reports 1.37x to 6.17x CPU speedups over full-precision baselines.
strengths: Reports 2.37x-6.17x speedups on x86 and 1.37x-5.07x on ARM versus full precision
Runs a 100B BitNet b1.58 model on one CPU at 5-7 tokens per second (per README)
Supports official 2B-4T and embedding models plus Falcon3, Falcon-E and Llama3-8B ternary variants
Includes an end-to-end benchmark script and a dummy-model generator
weaknesses: Only ternary 1-bit models are supported; ordinary GGUF models are out of scope
No HTTP server or OpenAI-compatible API described; usage is via run_inference.py CLI
Kernel support is uneven across models; embedding models have no ARM support
Build needs clang>=18, cmake>=3.22 and Python>=3.10; no Docker or release builds

projects.name: OpenLLM
projects.tagline: One-command OpenAI-compatible endpoints for curated open LLMs
projects.summary: OpenLLM serves open LLMs as OpenAI-compatible APIs with one command: pip install openllm, then openllm serve llama3.2:1b starts a vLLM-backed server on port 3000 with a chat UI at /chat. Models come as prebuilt Bentos from a curated repository (Llama 3.x and 4, Qwen2.5, Mistral, Phi-4, Gemma, DeepSeek R1) and the catalog states the GPU each needs. openllm deploy pushes the same Bento to BentoCloud.
strengths: One command gives an OpenAI API plus /chat UI on port 3000
Catalog lists the required GPU per model tag (12 GB to 16x80 GB)
vLLM backend for serving
Same Bento deploys to Docker, Kubernetes or BentoCloud
weaknesses: Every catalog model requires a GPU; no CPU-only entries
Custom model repositories must be public
Catalog tops out around Llama 3.3 and Qwen2.5; last commit 2026-05-29
Adding models means building BentoML Bentos

projects.name: llamafactory
projects.tagline: Fine-tuning toolkit for 100+ LLMs with a CLI and Gradio web UI
projects.summary: LlamaFactory fine-tunes language and multimodal models through YAML-configured CLI runs or the LLaMA Board Gradio UI. It covers pre-training, SFT, reward modeling, PPO, DPO, KTO and ORPO, with full-tuning, freeze-tuning, LoRA and 2 to 8-bit QLoRA. Trained models can be served through an OpenAI-style API using vLLM or SGLang workers.
strengths: Broad method coverage: SFT, PPO, DPO, KTO, ORPO, LoRA, QLoRA via AQLM/AWQ/GPTQ/HQQ/EETQ
Supports GaLore, BAdam, APOLLO, Muon, DoRA, PiSSA, plus Unsloth and Liger Kernel speedups
Covers multimodal and audio models such as Qwen3-VL, LLaVA and Qwen2-Audio
Runs on NVIDIA, AMD ROCm and Ascend NPU, with hosted Colab and PAI-DSW notebooks
weaknesses: Official documentation is marked WIP in the README
No VRAM or RAM figures in the visible README; hardware requirements unknown here
Web UI is for training and chat, not a production serving layer
Many optional backends (vLLM, SGLang, Unsloth, KTransformers) add install complexity

projects.name: deepspeed
projects.tagline: PyTorch library for distributed training of large models with ZeRO
projects.summary: DeepSpeed is a PyTorch optimization library for training large deep learning models across many GPUs. It provides ZeRO memory partitioning with CPU and NVMe offload, 3D parallelism, Ulysses sequence parallelism and MoE support, configured through a JSON file. It integrates with Hugging Face Transformers and Accelerate, Lightning, MosaicML Composer, Determined and MMEngine.
strengths: Used to train models such as BLOOM 176B and Megatron-Turing NLG 530B
Integrates with Hugging Face Transformers/Accelerate, Lightning, Composer, Determined and MMEngine
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Gaudi/XPU/CPU, Huawei Ascend NPU and Tecorigin accelerators
Installs from PyPI; C++/CUDA ops are JIT-compiled or pre-built
weaknesses: Needs PyTorch installed first and a CUDA or ROCm compiler for JIT ops
Mainly tested on NVIDIA Pascal to Hopper and AMD MI100/MI200
Windows lacks async IO and GDS support
Large JSON config surface; ZeRO and offload tuning requires reading the docs

projects.name: minimind
projects.tagline: Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in plain PyTorch
projects.summary: MiniMind is a from-scratch implementation of a small Qwen3-style decoder-only LLM (64M dense, 198M-A64M MoE) with each training stage written in native PyTorch: pretrain, SFT, LoRA, DPO, PPO/GRPO/CISPO, agentic RL and distillation. It ships datasets, a 6,400-token tokenizer, an OpenAI-compatible server and a Streamlit chat UI. The README states one SFT epoch takes about 2 hours on a single 3090.
strengths: Core algorithms (LoRA, DPO, PPO/GRPO) written in plain PyTorch, not wrapped from trl or peft
Open datasets for each stage, with mini variants (1.2GB pretrain, 1.6GB SFT) for quick runs
Weights convert to transformers, llama.cpp, vllm and ollama; ollama and vllm usage is documented
Checkpoint resume, DDP and DeepSpeed multi-GPU, wandb or swanlab logging
weaknesses: Models are tiny (64M), so output quality is far below mainstream LLMs
README is primarily in Chinese; the English version is a separate file
Training data is largely synthetic and distilled, with mixed source licenses
Native MoE training is about 50% slower than dense, per the README

projects.name: nanochat
projects.tagline: Minimal PyTorch codebase to train and chat with a small GPT-2-class LLM
projects.summary: nanochat covers tokenizer training, pretraining, SFT, RL, evaluation and a CLI chat interface in one small Python codebase. A single `--depth` setting derives width, heads, learning rate and training horizon, so one knob produces a compute-optimal model series. The reference speedrun trains a GPT-2-grade model in about 1.65 hours on an 8xH100 node per the leaderboard.
strengths: Covers tokenizer, pretraining, SFT, RL, eval and inference in one repo
Single `--depth` dial sets all other hyperparameters automatically
Public time-to-GPT-2 leaderboard with commits and CORE scores
Same scripts run on one GPU via gradient accumulation, or on CPU/MPS
weaknesses: Reference speedrun needs an 8xH100 node, roughly $48 of rented compute
Under 80GB VRAM requires manually lowering `--device-batch-size`
CPU/MPS path only trains a tiny model with weak results
Chat is CLI-only in the README; resulting model is small and hallucinates

projects.name: colossalai
projects.tagline: Distributed training library for large models with many parallelism strategies
projects.summary: Colossal-AI is a PyTorch-based library for training and running large models across multiple GPUs. It provides data, pipeline, 1D/2D/2.5D/3D tensor and sequence parallelism, ZeRO, auto-parallelism and heterogeneous memory management. The repo also hosts example applications such as Colossal-LLaMA-2, ColossalChat (RLHF) and Stable Diffusion acceleration, plus an inference module.
strengths: Covers data, pipeline, tensor (1D to 3D), sequence parallelism and ZeRO in one library
Published benchmarks for 7B and 70B Llama-like models on H200 and B200 GPUs
Includes worked applications: Colossal-LLaMA-2, ColossalChat RLHF, Stable Diffusion training
Apache-2.0 license, with a Dockerfile and PyPI install
weaknesses: Last tagged release is 2025-06-04, older than recent commits
README is heavily promotional for the vendor's GPU cloud and model APIs
Multi-GPU focus; RAM and minimum GPU requirements are not stated in the README
Many example sections are dated, with news items ending in 2025

projects.name: transformers
projects.tagline: Model-definition library for text, vision, audio and multimodal models
projects.summary: Transformers is a Python library that defines model architectures for text, vision, audio, video and multimodal models and loads pretrained checkpoints from the Hugging Face Hub. It offers a Pipeline API for inference, a PyTorch-based training API, and `transformers serve` and `transformers chat` commands. Other training frameworks and inference engines reuse its model definitions.
strengths: Hundreds of architectures and 1M+ Hub checkpoints behind one unified API
Pipeline API covers text, audio, vision and multimodal tasks in a few lines
Definitions are reused by Axolotl, Unsloth, DeepSpeed, vLLM, SGLang, TGI and others
Model files are deliberately flat and usable independently of the library
weaknesses: Not a modular toolbox of neural net building blocks, per the README
Training API targets Transformers' PyTorch models; generic loops should use Accelerate
Example scripts are only examples and may need adapting
Requires Python 3.10+ and PyTorch 2.6+; RAM and GPU needs are not stated

projects.name: pytorch
projects.tagline: Python tensor library with GPU support and tape-based autograd for deep learning
